SUMMARY
This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this
prospectus. Since it is a summary, it does not contain all the information that may be
importanttoyou.Youshouldreadthisprospectusinitsentiretybeforeyoudecidetoinvestin
the Offer Shares.
There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in
investing in the Offer Shares are set out in the section headed “Risk Factors.” You should
read that section carefully before you decide to invest in the Offer Shares.
OVERVIEW
We are a prominent player in the global electronic paper, or e-paper, display industry
mainlyengagedinthedevelopment,productionandsalesof e-paperdisplaymodules.Wewere
the second largest global e-paper display manufacturer by revenue in 2025, with a market
share of 20.8%, and the largest global commercial e-paper display manufacturer by revenue,
with a market share of 24.9%, according to CIC. The global commercial e-paper display
segment accounted for 83.5% of the overall global e-paper display market in 2025 in terms of
revenue, underscoring our market position in the industry.
Over the past 15 years, we have accumulated experience in the e-paper display industry
andbuiltcapabilitiesinproprietarydesignandmanufacturingof e-paperdisplaymodules.We
focus on the R&D, production and sales of a wide range of e-paper display modules covering
afullspectrumof displaycolorsandsizes.Ourproductportfolioisusedindiverseapplication
scenarios including smart retail, smart offices, smart education, smart logistics, smart
transportation, e-readers and emerging applications.
Below sets forth an illustration of the structure of our e-paper display modules as well
as their major end-applications:

End-applications of the E-paper Display Modules

Our e-paper display module constitutes the hardware set of an e-paper display
end-product, and it functions as a key component that converts data into image signals for
display on e-paper, ultimately driving the operation of the e-paper display end-product. Our
production process entails the cutting, lamination, bonding and dispensing of various raw
materials to assemble the final e-paper display modules which utilizes core e-paper display
technologies owned by third-party suppliers mainly with respect to raw materials such as
electronic ink films, or e-ink films. In the overall e-paper display value chain, our e-paper
display module can be viewed as a semi-finished product as it needs to be integrated into the
e-paper display end-product to deliver its full functionality. The e-paper display end-product
may take different forms depending on its downstream applications.

SUMMARY
Subject to customer specifications, most of the products sold by us during the Track
Record Period have a lifespan of generally five years. Subject to different customer
requirements, it usually takes around four to six months of lead time from product design to
delivery. Our product iteration process is driven by industry technological advancements,
evolving customer needs, and product upgrade roadmaps formulated and updated by us from
time to time. Core technologies for our products, such as upgrades in key e-paper materials
(e.g., e-ink films, driver integrated circuits and thin film transistor substrates), undergo a
major iteration cycle every two to three years. The outcomes of these iterations are
incorporated into both our existing and new products, ensuring the continuous advancement
of ourtechnologicalcompetitiveness.Weaimtoefficientlyadapttoevolvingneedsandtrends
through continuous product development and iteration, as well as constant interaction with
ourcustomersandinmeetingcustomerneedsindownstreamapplications.Forfurtherdetails,
see “Business — Our Strengths — Strong technical expertise and continuous innovation as
coredrivers”,“Business—OurStrategies—Continuetoinvestintechnologicalinnovationto
expand our product portfolio”, “Business — Our Technologies and Research and
Development” and “Business — Applications of our Products — Capability to adapt to
product iteration and expand downstream applications.” According to CIC, we have been
historicallyattheforefrontof,orkeptpacewith,ourindustrypeercompaniesinthelaunchof
advanced or upgraded products (such as three-color and four-color products).
As a prominent player in the global e-paper display industry, we continuously pursue
R&D and innovation to strengthen our core competitiveness. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, we held 98 patents, including 32 invention patents, solidifying the technology
capabilities to support the expansion of our product portfolio. Going forward, we will
continue to invest in the R&D of new and enhanced products such as flexible, full-color and
ultra-large displays, further enriching our offerings and delivering more advanced,
high-quality products for our customers and the industry.
Our global footprint
Toefficientlyserveourglobalcustomers,wehaveestablishedfourproductionandR&D
bases,beingthelargestnumberamongindustryplayersworldwideasof theLatestPracticable
Date according to CIC, together with multiple offices across China and overseas, which
provide comprehensive customer service targeting markets in Europe, America, Asia, among
others. Leveraging our localized presence, we continuously optimize supply chain and
logistics costs for our customers, ensuring agile and reliable response to their needs.
Our market opportunities and competition
As the world accelerates its transition towards green and low-carbon development,
demandfordigitalizationandpaperlessdisplayscontinuestorise.Amongmainstreamdisplay
technologies, e-paper stands out with unique advantages — ultra-low power consumption,
paper-like texture, eye-friendly experience, thinness, shatter resistance and bendability.
Compared with liquid-crystal display (“LCD”) and organic light-emitting diodes (“OLED”),
which rely heavily on backlighting and consume more energy, e-paper is inherently better
suitedtotheevolutionof smartIoTterminals.Itsultra-lowpowerprofilealsoalignswellwith
the objective of global carbon-neutral strategy.
Withcontinuedpolicysupportforlow-carbondigitalinfrastructure,progressinflexible
e-paper enabled by organic thin film transistor (“OTFT”) technology, and the growing
demand for flexible, energy-efficient display technologies in smart IoT devices, we believe
e-paper is poised to penetrate a wider range of commercial and consumer applications in the
years to come.
With ongoing advances in technology and the broadening of application scenarios,
e-paper has evolved beyond its traditional uses in smart retail and e-reading, steadily
expanding into a variety of emerging industries and niche markets. This expansion not only
fuels sustained growth across the sector but also creates significant opportunities for us.
– 4 –

=== PAGE 14 ===
SUMMARY
Againstthisbackdrop,theglobalretailindustryisacceleratingitsdigitaltransformation,
with electronic shelf labels gaining wider adoption. According to CIC, the global market for
e-paper display in smart retail is expected to reach 803.2 million units by 2030, with a CAGR
of 11.2% from 2025 to 2030. At the same time, fast-growing sectors such as smart education,
smart offices and smart logistics are opening up new opportunities, with e-paper increasingly
applied in areas such as warehouse management systems and interactive smart home displays
— further driving market demand. According to CIC, the global market for e-paper related
products is projected to grow from RMB74.0 billion in 2025 to RMB111.7 billion in 2030,
representing a CAGR of 8.6%.
In 2025, the global e-paper display market remained highly concentrated. Leading
players, leveraging years of technological development, market experience and product
validation, have established diversified product portfolios encompassing monochrome,
multi-color, full-color, flexible and segment-type products. These are widely deployed across
commercial and consumer applications, including retail, industrial, healthcare and consumer
electronics. With a recovery in downstream demand — particularly for e-paper price tags —
industry inventory levels have been rapidly reduced, and sales volumes have become
increasingly concentrated among top-tier suppliers, resulting in a stable yet increasingly
consolidated competitive landscape.
We have demonstrated strong market competitiveness. We were the second largest
global e-paper display manufacturer by revenue in 2025, with a market share of 20.8%, and
thelargestglobalcommerciale-paperdisplaymanufacturerbyrevenue,withamarketshareof
24.9%, according to CIC. Notably, according to CIC, we are one of the few players globally
with a first-mover advantage in the field of flexible e-paper technology and mass
commercialization. For commercial e-paper display, our product portfolio spans full-size,
full-color and flexible formats, with diverse and flexible delivery models. Furthermore, we
were the first company globally to deploy e-paper display products in the intelligent robotics
sector, achieving an edge in both technological innovation and real-world commercial
deployment, thereby establishing a competitive advantage.
We intend to continue investing in technological development, refining our
customer-focusedsolutions,andimprovingoperationalefficiency.Atthesametime,wewould
remain mindful of the dynamic nature of market competition. Competition may come from
existing players and new entrants, including our customers and suppliers who may have
enteredorarecontemplatingtoestablishproductionfore-paperdisplaymodules.Forfurther
details,see“RiskFactors—RisksrelatingtoOurBusinessandIndustry—Weareconfronted
withcompetitionfromotherindustryplayersandthepressureof technologicaliteration.”See
also “Industry Overview — Overview of Competition in the Global E-Paper Display
Industry.”
Our financial and business performance
Buildingonyearsof industryexperienceandbusinesscapabilities,wehavecontinuedto
deliver steady progress in both scale and operational efficiency. Sales of our e-paper display
modules increased from 56.1 million units in 2023 to 67.1 million units in 2024 and further to
124.5 million units in 2025. During the Track Record Period, we maintained substantial
investment in R&D, achieving a CAGR of 21.6% in R&D spending from 2023 to 2025. In
2023, 2024 and 2025, our revenue was RMB1,024.2 million, RMB1,151.6 million and
RMB1,713.0 million, respectively, and our profit for the year was RMB50.7 million,
RMB53.4 million and RMB80.2 million, respectively.
We have launched new e-paper display products, including full-color, large-size
billboard products. Our product pipeline also includes small- and medium-sized full-color
OTFT, PI a-Si and other flexible products, full-color, large-size products powered by Spectra
6 technology, as well as multi-color, wide-temperature products powered by Spectra 3100
technology. With these innovations, our application scenarios are extending beyond smart
retail into smart office, smart education, smart logistics, smart transportation and smart
healthcare, unlocking significant revenue growth potential.

SUMMARY
OUR SALES NETWORK
We primarily conduct our sales through a direct sales model globally, and promote our
products and expand our customer base through industry referrals, participation in trade
exhibitions, sales team outreach and online marketing. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue from
our direct sales was RMB997.6 million, RMB1,127.6 million and RMB1,686.6 million,
respectively, representing 97.4%, 97.9% and 98.4% of our total revenue, respectively. To a
much lesser extent, we also conduct our sales through distributors. For details, see “Business
— Sales and Marketing — Our Sales Network.”
During the Track Record Period, our sales to customers domiciled in China and
Vietnam in aggregate accounted for a substantial portion of our revenue whereas revenue
contribution from customers domiciled in other countries or regions was relatively limited
individually. For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue generated from
customers in China accounted for 26.6%, 36.7% and 55.0% of our total revenue, respectively,
and revenue generated from customers in Vietnam accounted for 50.7%, 36.2% and 31.9% of
our total revenue, respectively. For further details, see “Business — Sales and Marketing —
Revenue by Customer Location.”
OUR CUSTOMERS
During the Track Record Period, our customers primarily included leading global and
domestic providers of smart retail and IoT display solutions. These customers focus on areas
such as electronic shelf labels, retail automation, in-store digitalization, digital technology
integration, e-paper price tags and related applications. They generally maintain stringent
supplier qualification standards, requiring high levels of product quality, reliability and
compliance.In2023,2024and2025,revenuegeneratedfromourfivelargestcustomersineach
year during the Track Record Period was RMB908.4 million, RMB950.9 million and
RMB1,555.0 million, respectively, representing 88.7%, 82.6% and 90.8% of our total revenue,
respectively.
Solum, a company listed on the Korea Exchange (stock code: 248070) as of the Latest
Practicable Date, specializing in power modules, digital tuners, electronic shelf labels and
other electronic components and solutions, was our largest customer for 2023 and 2024 and
the second largest customer for 2025. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our revenue from Solum was
RMB519.6 million, RMB417.7 million and RMB495.1 million, respectively, representing
50.7%,36.3%and28.9%,respectively,of ourtotalrevenueforthesameyears.Inaddition,our
revenue from our largest customer for 2025, Customer A, was RMB48.7 million, RMB168.4
millionandRMB605.6millionin2023,2024and2025,respectively,representing4.7%,14.6%
and 35.4% of our total revenue, respectively. Any termination, material interruption or
adverse modification of our relationship with Solum, Customer A or similar major
customer(s), could have a material adverse effect on our operations and financial
performance.
Our Directors do not expect that our major customers will materially reduce the
amounts of purchase from us. Moreover, leveraging our sales and marketing efforts to seize
new business opportunities and our strong customer base, our Directors consider that if we
were to lose any major customer in the future, any adverse impact on our financial
performance would not be expected to be permanent. We have taken several measures to
mitigate our concentration risks. For more details, see “Business — Our Customers —
Customer Concentration”and “Risk Factors — Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry
— We had a concentration of customers during the Track Record Period.”

(c) our supplier concentration exposes us to supply chain risks, the loss of which could

customer base, or increasing sales to existing customers, our business, operating results and

business, and we may incur substantial expenses to protect our intellectual property rights,
and (g) our historical results may not be indicative of our business, operating results and
financial condition, and we may not be able to manage future growth effectively.

four-color product to gradually replace three-color products as the primary product type
targeting the smart retail sector. For further details of changes during the Track Record
Period in our sales of e-paper display modules (including sales volume and average selling
price) by size and by display color, see “Financial Information — Principal Components of
Consolidated Statements of Profit or Loss and Historical Results of Operations — Revenue
— Sales Volume and Average Selling Price.” According to CIC, the selling prices of our
products were generally in line with the market prices during the Track Record Period.
According to CIC, three-color products remain the mainstream in the global e-paper
displayindustryduetoamorematuresupplychainandrelativelylowercosts,whilefour-color
products, driven by the ongoing shift toward color, offer stronger capabilities in information
encoding and promotional presentation. Compared to three-color products of either the
combination of black/white/red or black/white/yellow, four-color products have richer color
performance covering all such four colors to enable more differentiated and targeted content
displayformorepreciseandnuancedinformationpresentation.Forinstance,inretailsettings
of ESLs, black can indicate the original price, red can be used to highlight the promotional
priceandyellowcanbeforfurtherinformationsuchasproductspecificationsorpromotional
terms. The introduction of the additional color dimension helps enhance visual experience
and marketing impact. Moreover, four-color products also feature improvements in refresh
rate and adaptability to a wider temperature range, making them suitable for more complex
scenarios in smart retail and smart home, etc.
– 12 –

=== PAGE 22 ===
SUMMARY
For e-paper display modules, the different combination of module size and number of
colors for display primarily depends on the requirements of different downstream
applications.Forinstance,ESLs,whichneedtodisplayproductdiversityandattractcustomer
attention to key items, tend to favor multi-color displays as opposed to monochrome (black
and white) displays. In contrast, industrial control applications, which place greater demands
on response speed, temperature range and other industrial performance metrics not heavily
hinging on colourful visual impact, tend to prefer monochrome displays. Separately, in terms
of module size, the smart retail sector in general utilizes small-size e-paper display modules
(such as in the case of ESLs) whereas sectors such as smart transportation and smart
education typically utilize larger-size modules.

periods; and (b) employee benefits expenses which were RMB79.8 million, RMB78.3 million
and RMB112.7 million, respectively, representing 9.3%, 8.1% and 7.9% of our cost of sales,
respectively, and which increased from RMB79.8 million in 2023 to RMB112.7 million in
2025, as we expanded our production capacities during the Track Record Period.

DIVIDENDS
We declared and paid dividends of RMB23.0 million in 2024. Other than that, no
dividend was declared or paid by our Company or any of our subsidiaries during the Track
Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date. Our dividend distribution record in the
past may not be used as a reference or basis to determine the level of dividends that may be
declared or paid by us in the future. Currently, our Group does not have a formal dividend
policy and does not have a predetermined dividend distribution ratio.
After completion of the Global Offering, we may distribute dividends in the form of
cash or by other means permitted by our Articles of Association. Any proposed distribution
of dividends shall be formulated by our Board and will be subject to approval of our
Shareholders. A decision to declare or to pay any dividends in the future, and the amount of
any dividend, will depend upon a number of factors, including our earnings and financial
condition, operating requirements, capital requirements, business prospects, statutory,
regulatoryandcontractualrestrictionsonourdeclarationandpaymentof dividends,andany
other factors that our Directors may consider important.
AsadvisedbyourPRCLegalAdvisorsandaccordingtothePRCCompanyLaw,aPRC
incorporated company is required to set aside at least 10% of its after-tax profits each year,
after making up previous years’accumulated losses, if any, to contribute to certain statutory
reserve funds until the aggregate amount contributed to such funds reaches 50% of its
registered capital. Such company may pay dividends out of after-tax profits after making up
for accumulated losses and contributing to statutory reserve funds as mentioned above.
As confirmed by our PRC Legal Advisors, according to relevant PRC laws, any future
netprofitthatourCompanyoranyof ourPRCsubsidiariesmakewillhavetobefirstapplied
to make up for any historically accumulated losses, after which we will be obliged to allocate
10% of net profit to our statutory common reserve fund until such fund has reached more
than50%of ourregisteredcapital.Wewillthereforeonlybeabletodeclaredividendsafter(i)
all our historically accumulated losses (if any) have been made up for; and (ii) we have
allocated sufficient net profit to our statutory common reserve fund as described above.

“8D Report” a structured problem-solving report used in manufacturing
and quality management to address and correct defects. It
documents the eight disciplines: Team formation, Problem
description, Containment actions, Root cause analysis,
Corrective actions, Implementation, Preventive measures and
Congratulation/Closure. Widely used in e-paper display
production to resolve recurring issues and improve quality
“ACeP” Advanced Color ePaper, a full-color e-paper display
technology developed by E Ink that enables each pixel to
produce a wide color gamut using a single layer of
electrophoretic ink. ACeP achieves color rendering through
electronically controlled pigment movement, offering high
visibility, low power consumption and a reflective, paper-like
appearance suitable for applications such as signage and
information displays
“ACF” anisotropic conductive film, a film-type adhesive material
containing conductive particles, which enables electrical
conductivity primarily in one direction while remaining
electrically insulating in other directions. It is used to form
electrical and mechanical connections between components in
the assembly of electronic paper display modules and other
electronic products
“AOI” automated optical inspection, a kind of technology that uses
cameras and image processing to detect defects or verify
quality in electronic assemblies
“black-and-white e-paper e-paper display modules supporting black and white colors
display module” only
“COG” chip-on-glass, a packaging technology in which an integrated
circuit chip is directly mounted and electrically connected
onto the glass substrate of an e-paper display. This method
reducesmodulethicknessandimproveselectricalperformance
“Class 1,000 cleanroom” Class1,000cleanroomreferstoacleanroomwherethenumber
of particles ≥ 0.5 microns does not exceed 1,000 per cubic foot
of air,makingittentimescleanerthanClass10,000cleanroom

air

RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY
Thee-paperdisplayindustryinwhichweoperateischaracterizedbyconstantchanges.If wefail
to provide innovative products that meet customers’ evolving needs, continuously improve our
technology, maintain our technological edge and achieve tangible results from our R&D efforts,
our business, operating results and financial condition will be materially and adversely affected.
The e-paper display industry has been rapidly changing and evolving and has been
driven at various times by the emergence and development of other display technologies, as
well as the widespread adoption of other digital smart terminals. Companies in the e-paper
display industry have aggressively expanded production capacity in recent years to meet the
market demands. If actual demand from downstream players such as e-paper application
providers does not grow as expected or declines, or if the industry experiences technological
iteration that shifts market demand, the entire industry will typically go through a period
where capacity exceeds demand. However, if industry-wide capacity exceeds demand, our
operations would be subject to more intense competition, and our results of operations may
suffer because of the resulting pricing pressure and capacity underutilization. Severe pricing
pressure could result in the overall industry becoming less profitable, at least for the duration
of the downturn, and could prevent us from maintaining profitability. For instance, we have
experiencedacontinuousreductioninthesellingpricesof oure-paperdisplaymodulesduring
the Track Record Period, such as those in relation to our three-color and four-color products
of varioussizes.Wecannotguaranteeif suchdownwardpricingtrendcouldbeimprovedorif
we could maintain the profitability of the relevant products in the future.
We have made continuous investments in R&D to build our R&D capabilities. Our
R&D expenses amounted to RMB39.9 million, RMB56.0 million and RMB59.0 million for
the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, representing 3.9%, 4.9% and
3.4% of our total revenue for the respective periods. The e-paper display industry is
undergoing rapid development with respect to technological advancement and product
iterationandthemarketconcentrationisexpectedtocontinuetorise.Duetotherapidpaceof
product iteration in the industry, we cannot guarantee that we can always adapt our R&D to
these trends, successfully launch, commercialize and iterate our products in a timely and
commercially viable manner to prevent any product obsolescence, or meet our R&D goals on
schedule and within budget. Simultaneously, our competitors are actively developing new
technologies.Shouldtheyoutpaceus,theirinnovationscouldgivethemaperformanceorcost
advantage, potentially eroding our competitive position. If any of these events occur, our
business,operatingresultsandfinancialconditioncouldbemateriallyandadverselyaffected.

addressforeignexchangevolatilitythroughoperationalnaturalhedgingstrategies,reasonably
matching foreign currency-denominated revenues with related expenses to reduce net foreign

currency assets and liabilities as well as exchange rate trends, and will, in response to changes
in market conditions and actual operational needs, timely evaluate and employ appropriate
risk management tools to further prudently manage exchange rate risks. Nonetheless,

profit margin, and may also result in foreign exchange losses.

OVERVIEW OF THE GLOBAL FLAT PANEL DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY
The current mainstream display technologies employed in tablets primarily fall into
four categories: electronic paper, liquid crystal display (LCD), light emitting diode (LED),
and organic light emitting diode (OLED). 1) Operating on electrophoretic or electrochromic
principles, e-paper reflects ambient light to form an image, eliminating the need for a
backlight.Itischaracterizedbyitspaper-likequality,sunlightreadability,andbendability.Its
power consumption is exceptionally low, being nearly zero in a static state and only required
during screen refreshes, making it significantly more efficient than other technologies.
Furthermore, as it is not self-emissive, it produces no blue light and has no flicker, offering
superior eye comfort. This technology can be integrated with flexible substrates, making it
suitable for rollable, thin, and lightweight smart device form factors. 2) LCDs function by
controllingthepassageof aseparatebacklightthroughliquidcrystalmoleculestoproducean
image. They offer the advantages of mature manufacturing processes, low cost, and display
stability, cementing their status as the most widely adopted display technology currently
available. 3) An emissive technology, LED displays form images through a matrix of
high-density point light sources. They are known for high brightness and long viewing
distances, making them the predominant solution for large-format outdoor display scenarios.
4) OLED technology uses organic compounds that emit light upon electrical excitation. It
provideshighcontrastratios,wideviewingangles,andfastresponsetimes.Itskeyadvantages
include exceptional contrast, rapid response, and inherent support for flexibility, securing its
position as the leading technology for high-end mobile devices and wearable devices.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Traditional flat panel displays predominantly serve mainstream consumer electronics.
In contrast, e-paper is primarily deployed in commercial and enterprise applications, such as
electronic shelf labels (ESLs) and digital signage. In these commercial environments,
large-scaledeploymentof LCDorOLEDscreensisgenerallycost-prohibitiveandimpractical
due to higher unit costs, constant power consumption, and susceptibility to screen burn-in.
E-paper perfectly addresses these commercial needs through superior cost-effectiveness,
ultra-low power consumption (bistable display), and long-term durability.
Within the consumer electronics sector, LCD, LED, and OLED technologies dominate
themassmarketbyfulfillingdemandsforhighcontrast,vibrantcolors,andhighrefreshrates.
E-paper, however, targets a specific, complementary niche focused on eye protection,
paper-like reading and writing experiences, and extended battery life. These specialized user
needs cannot be effectively met by standard light-emitting displays.
Given their distinct technological characteristics, e-paper and traditional flat panel
displays serve different market segments. Rather than competing directly, they act as
complementary technologies within the broader display industry, making the threat of
substitution from LCD, LED, and OLED products inherently limited.
In comparison to alternative display solutions, e-paper holds significant advantages in
power consumption management, eye-comfort, and environmental sustainability. These
characteristics make it particularly well-suited for smart devices where energy efficiency and
persistent display capabilities are paramount. Currently, e-paper technology is already
extensively deployed across a diverse range of applications, including smart retail, smart
office, smart education, smart logistics, smart transportation, e-readers, and other emerging
use cases. Its operational profile aligns perfectly with the strategic shift towards green and
low-carbon technologies in the smart device sector, strongly supporting the global “carbon
neutrality”objectives.Lookingforward,ascolorandflexibledisplaytechnologiescontinueto
achieve breakthroughs, e-paper is expected to achieve further penetration in more advanced
applicationscenarios,includingdigitalwallets,curveddisplays,andflexiblewearabledevices.
Amid a competitive landscape of coexisting display technologies, e-paper tablets are
achieving steadily increasing penetration within the global market for static application.
Measured by sales, their market penetration rate of the global static application market has
increased from 8.3% in 2021 to 12.9% by 2025. This growth is being driven by sustained
demand across key application scenarios such as electronic shelf labels, paperless office
products, smart transportation systems, and other low-power devices. As these sectors
continuetoexpand,e-paperiswell-positionedforlarge-scaleadoptionacrossanevenbroader
range of downstream applications. Consequently, its market penetration of the global static
application market is forecast to rise further, reaching 13.0% by 2030.
OVERVIEW OF THE GLOBAL E-PAPER RELATED SOLUTION INDUSTRY
Definition and Classification of E-Paper Related Solution Industry
E-paper related solution impart interactive capabilities to smart devices, allowing them
to simulate human sensory functions to achieve environmental perception, information
comprehension, and user interaction. The ecosystem for these solutions encompasses e-paper
display e-paper, application and supporting services, delivering a fully integrated hardware
and software package. In contrast to traditional LCD, LED, and OLED solutions, e-paper
relatedsolutionconsumeanegligibleamountof energyonlyduringscreenrefreshes.Oncean
image is updated, it is maintained indefinitely with zero or ultra-low power draw, drastically
reducing overall energy consumption. Furthermore, due to its use of ambient light reflection
—muchliketraditionalpaper—thistechnologyprovidesacomfortablereadingexperience,is
ultra-thin and lightweight, and can be viewed for extended periods without causing visual
fatigue.
– 72 –

=== PAGE 82 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
E-paper related solution are categorized primarily by their size and display
characteristics, with size classifications typically segmented into small (<4 inches),
medium-to-large (4-6 inches), and large (>6 inches) displays, each suited to distinct
application scenarios, while display performance is differentiated by color capability,
including monochrome, three/four-color, and multi-color variants, each offering specific
characteristics in terms of power consumption, refresh rate, and overall suitability for
particular use cases.
Technological Development Paths and Trends in the E-Paper Related Solution Industry
At its core, the display technology underpinning e-paper related solution is a reflective,
passive technology, which relies on ambient light for visibility. It is non-emissive, and only
consumes power when updating the image. Its fundamental operating principle involves
modulating the reflection and absorption of ambient light to achieve a reading experience
virtually indistinguishable from that of traditional paper.
Current R&D in e-paper technology is primarily focused on three key directions: color
performance, medium-to-large sized displays, and flexible screen applications. In color
display,themainstreamapplicationcurrentlycentersonthree-andfour-colorschemes,which
arepredominantlyusedinelectronicshelf labelsandhaverecentlybeguntoexpandintosmart
retail and smart office. Regarding size, evolving application demanding higher information
capacity and expanded interactive scenarios are driving a shift from small displays towards
medium and large-sized panels, consequently expanding their use from price tags into
advertisingsignageandothers.Inflexibledisplays,leveragingtheinnateflexibilityof e-paper
film by substituting glass substrates with flexible alternatives enables the development of
bendable and foldable applications, thereby unlocking new possibilities for wearable
technology and foldable screen applications.

tiers. The upstream sector supplies E-ink film, TFT substrates, driver integrated circuits, and
other core components and raw materials of e-paper related solutions industry. The
midstream sector focuses on the manufacturing and service of E-Paper related solutions,
transforming upstream materials and components into display solutions, then manufacturing
them into E-Paper devices, ultimately providing stable products and services to the
downstream customers in commercial sector and consumer sector. Within the midstream, the

Optoelectronics, Xingtai Technology, Yes Optoelectronics, etc. The downstream sector
includes application scenarios, spanning commercial fields such as smart retail, smart office,
smart education, smart logistics, and smart transportation, as well as consumer-facing
products like e-book readers and other emerging applications.

Market Drivers of E-paper Display Industry
• Accelerated technological iteration and enhanced product capability: The
production processes for e-paper display are undergoing continuous refinement,
leading to consistent breakthroughs in production yield. This advancement
effectively reduces unit costs and is fostering the development of a more
standardized supply chain, which collectively propels their large-scale adoption
across downstream applications. Concurrently, breakthroughs in the technology,
spanning dimensions such as size, display characteristics, and flexibility, are
enabling diversification of their applications. Use cases are expanding beyond
traditional e-readers and price tags into a growing number of emerging sectors,
including smart transportation and smart logistics. This ongoing diversification
is providing sustained impetus for market growth.
• Supportive policies drive green display technology and market development:
GovernmentsinEurope,NorthAmerica,andChinahavesuccessivelyannounced
clear carbon neutrality and carbon peak targets, providing both policy and
financial support for green display technologies. Europe is promoting the
adoption of low-power consumption display technologies, such as e-paper,
through its Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes. The United States
leverages standards such as the Electronic Product Environmental Assessment
Tool (EPEAT) to guide enterprises in developing low-energy, recyclable e-paper
technologies.InChina,underpinnedbyits“dualcarbon”goals,multiplepolicies
have been introduced to support the e-paper industry. For example, the “Notice
on Issuing the Action Plan for Steady Growth in the Electronic Information
Manufacturing Industry (2023-2024)”《( 關於印發電子信息製造業2023-2024年穩
增長行動方案的通知》) explicitly includes e-paper as a key solution for paperless
substitution, encouraging the adoption of green technology in retail, education,
and other scenarios and further proposes to promote the application of e-paper
innewsmartterminal,culture,tourism,landscapeandcommercialdisplayfields,
and to support e-paper in accelerating paperless substitution applications.
Furthermore, the “Outline of the Strategy for Expanding Domestic Demand
(2022-2035)” 《( 擴大內需戰略規劃綱要(2022-2035年)》) emphasized innovation
and application in new display technologies.

Market Trends of E-Paper Display Industry
• Rapidly growing downstream demand for medium and large-sized e-paper, and
continuously expanding new application scenarios: The current market is still
predominantly characterized by small-sized products such as price label and name tag,
etc, which accounted for 89.1% of the global sales volume for e-paper display in 2025.
However, fuelled by rising downstream requirements for greater information capacity
and cost reductions achieved through economies of scale, medium and large-sized
products are emerging as a critical growth driver for the e-paper industry. These larger
displays combine reading comfort with adaptability, finding broad application
potential in emerging fields such as retail price tags, smart transportation, and smart
logistics, which are mainly medium to large-sized e-paper application scenarios. From
2025to2030,theglobalmarketformediumandlarge-sizede-paperdisplayisprojected
toachieveaCAGRof 36.8%,withitsvolumeexpandingfrom56.9millionunitsin2025
to 272.5 million units in 2030.
• Technological evolution centers on colorization, video capability, flexibility, and deep
smart devices integration: Beyond traditional black/ white/ red and black/ white/ yellow
tri-color e-paper, the industry has successfully developed technologies supporting four
to six color, as well as multi-color capabilities based on platforms such as ACeP in
recent years, demonstrating a clear and sustained trend towards advanced color
performance.Furthermore,productsmanufacturedusingflexiblesubstratespossessthe
capability to bend and fold, aligning perfectly with emerging consumer demands for
foldable screens and wearable technology. In the age of smart devices, the inherent
characteristics of ultra-low power consumption and wireless updating allow these
products to remotely refresh pricing or inventory information in retail stores,
dynamically update departure information in smart transportation systems, and
visually synchronize temperature, humidity, and routing data in smart logistics,
solidifying their status as a preferred display for smart devices.
• Increasingmarketconcentrationwithleadingplayersgainingmoreprominentadvantages:
Firstly, technological barriers to entry continue to rise. Established players have
constructedaformidableintellectualpropertymoatthroughextensivepatentportfolios
covering critical components such as e-ink film, driver integrated circuits, and TFT
substrates. Secondly, the advantages of economies of scale are becoming increasingly
pronounced. Leading manufacturers achieve substantial cost reductions through
verticalintegrationof theirsupplychainsandtheimplementationof highlyautomated
production lines. Finally, downstream manufacturers, particularly those in the
commercial sector, exhibit a strong preference for partnering with major suppliers that
can guarantee consistent product quality and reliable delivery.

Market Drivers of E-Paper Application Industry
• The imperative for low-carbon energy efficiency and extended battery life. Against the
backdropof theglobalpushfor“CarbonNeutrality”strategicgoals,thereisastringent
requirement for electronic devices to drastically reduce their energy consumption. The
ultra-lowpowerconsumptioncharacteristicof e-paperapplicationperfectlyalignswith
this market imperative. Consequently, e-paper application are positioned as the ideal
technological pathway to replace traditional high-power display and propel green,
low-carbon transformation across numerous industries.
• A virtuous cycle driven by technological maturation and ecosystem expansion. In recent
years,e-paperapplicationhaveachievedsignificantbreakthroughsinrefreshrate,color
performance, and flexible/bendable form factors, substantially broadening their
application boundaries. The maturation of technology has lowered the barriers to
application, while the expansion of the ecosystem has stimulated innovative vitality.
The virtuous cycle formed by these two factors is collectively driving the industry
towards greater diversification and scale.

Market Trends of E-Paper Application Industry
• The trend towards larger sizes and colorization. Commercial e-paper application are
reshaping the business display ecosystem through technological breakthroughs in
medium/large-sizedformatsandcolorperformance.Regardinglargersizes,theindustry
is moving beyond the traditional application boundaries of e-paper. Leading players,
through optimized display technology and production processes, have achieved
breakthroughs in mass production. This enables these larger application to meet the
demands of diverse scenarios such as retail shelf labels and conference room displays,
significantly increasing information capacity while simultaneously reducing
deployment and maintenance costs. In terms of colorization, the evolution from
three/four-color systems towards multi-color technology has resulted in a display
quality that much more closely resembles printed material, dramatically enhancing the
visual experience and marketing impact.
• Thetrendtowardshigh-value-addedproducts.Thecommerciale-paperapplicationsector

penetration rates.
Threats and Challenges of Global E-paper Display Industry
• Supply chain concentration and scale-driven cost and supply pressure. Suppliers of core
materials and key technologies in the e-paper module industry are relatively
concentrated, creating sector-wide uncertainty in pricing, capacity and licensing.
Smaller players, with weaker scale and bargaining power, are more exposed to adverse
changes in procurement costs, supply allocation and technical support, leading to
greater earnings volatility.
• Customerconcentrationandqualificationbarriers.Downstreamcustomershasstringent
requirements on reliability, delivery and global service, and long qualification
processes. Smaller manufacturers often rely on a limited number of key customers,
making them more vulnerable if those customers change procurement strategies or
switch suppliers. Market leaders, supported by stronger brand recognition, extensive
track records and a more diversified customer base, are generally better positioned to
withstand such concentration risk.
• Technology evolution and product upgrade pressures on R&D. The Global E-paper
Display Industry is moving towards color, larger sizes and higher refresh rates, which
raises technical requirements in display driving, mechanical design and system
integration,andcallsforcontinuousR&Dandcapitalinvestment.Smallerplayerswith
limitedR&Dresources,fundingandtechnologicalaccumulationmaybedisadvantaged
inproductupgradecyclesandcostcontrol,facinghigherrisksof technologicallagand
margin compression. Leading companies with stronger technology reserves and the
ability to sustain R&D spending generally have greater flexibility in managing product
roadmaps and absorbing related risks.

OVERVIEW OF COMPETITION IN THE GLOBAL E-PAPER DISPLAY INDUSTRY
Competitive Landscape of the Global E-Paper Display Industry
In 2025, the global e-paper display industry demonstrated a high degree of market
concentration, with the top five market players accounting for approximately 82.0% of the
totalmarketsharebysales.Throughyearsof marketcultivationandproductvalidation,these
leading manufacturers have developed diversified product portfolios encompassing a wide
range of e-paper display, including monochrome, multi-color, flexible, and segment code and
prism, which are extensively deployed across various application scenarios in both
commercial and consumer end-markets. Recently, with the recovery in demand for
downstream electronic shelf label applications, major manufacturers have rapidly reduced
inventory levels. While the competitive landscape has remained stable, market share has
become further concentrated towards these leading players.
Currently, within the global e-paper display industry, manufacturers from Chinese
Mainland and Taiwan, China hold a dominant position. Notably, Chinese Mainland
manufacturers account for over 90% of this share. As downstream application demand
continues to expand, industry shipments are expected to become further concentrated with
leading Chinese Mainland manufacturers.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Entry Barriers in the E-Paper Display Industry
• Barriers of customer resources of leading players. Within the global e-paper display
industry, leading companies have established a dominant position in terms of revenue,
customer coverage, and brand recognition, leveraging their first-mover advantage and
economiesof scale.Theircustomerbaseencompassesmajorglobalbrandsandchannel
partners, with whom they maintain long-term, stable collaborative relationships. This
extensive and highly loyal client network not only ensures steady growth for existing
businessbutalsoprovidestheseleadingplayerswithanaturaladvantagewhenpursuing
new potential partnerships, further reinforcing their formidable customer resource
barriers.
• Barriers of industrial chain synergies. Within the global e-paper display industry,
leading players have established significant synergistic advantages through deep,
strategic partnerships with key upstream material suppliers and core downstream
customers. Conversely, leading downstream brand customers demonstrate a strong
preference for deep collaboration during the new product introduction phase,
facilitating rapid market validation and scalable deployment. This end-to-end
synergistic advantage throughout the entire industrial chain equips leading companies
withthecapabilitytomaintaincontinuousleadershipinbothestablishedandemerging
markets, creating a formidable barrier that is exceptionally difficult for potential new
entrants to overcome.
• Barriers of supply chain management. An advanced, efficient, and stable supply chain
management system is critical for suppliers of e-paper display. Leading players in the
sector have established dedicated supply chain management centers, creating a
comprehensive, multi-dimensional system that encompasses supplier evaluation, raw
material procurement, and quality testing. Furthermore, leveraging their stable
customer base and strong industry standing, these leading players are typically able to
negotiate more favorable commercial terms with core customers regarding delivery and
payment cycles. This includes securing shorter payment terms and achieving rapid
fulfillment of large-volume orders, thereby significantly enhancing their working
capital liquidity and operational stability.
• Barriers of cost control and efficiency optimisation. The e-paper display industry is
characterized by high economies of scale and significant cost sensitivity. Leading
enterprises, leveraging years of accumulated experience, have established sophisticated
production management systems and process optimisation capabilities. They achieve
substantial unit cost reductions through volume purchasing, automated production
lines, and improved production yields. Furthermore, these leading players engage in
joint development with customers during the R&D phase to reduce trial-and-error
costs,implementflexiblemanufacturingandsupplychaincollaborationtoenablerapid
changeovers and efficient delivery during production, and utilize their stable customer
relationships to shorten payment cycles.
• Barriers of core technology and independent R&D capability. The e-paper display sector
is a technology-intensive industry characterized by rapid iterative development, which
places significant demands on a company’s R&D prowess and process expertise.
Through long-term accumulation, leading enterprises in the industry have established
systematic R&D platforms and comprehensive patent portfolios. This foundation not
only enables them to effectively control production yields, operational efficiency, and
raw material utilization in mass production but also allows for sustained investment in
cutting-edge fields such as novel driving architectures, flexible display materials, and
low-powerconsumptiontechnologies.Thissustainedadvantagefurthersolidifiesadual
barrier encompassing both advanced technology and superior research and
development capabilities.
– 84 –

=== PAGE 94 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
• Barriers of capacity and intelligent quality control system. Production efficiency,
product quality, and economies of scale are of critical importance to manufacturers of
e-paper display. Leading players leverage expanded production capacity to amortize
fixed R&D costs, creating a significant price advantage and ultimately establishing a
virtuous cycle of “capacity driving orders, and orders justifying further capacity
expansion.” Concurrently, mature process systems and intelligent production
workflows are essential to effectively manage the quality and precision challenges
inherent in the mass production of e-paper module products across various size
specifications.
• Barriers of organizational management and digital capability. The e-paper display
industry is characterized by rapid technological iteration and high customer demand
for customisation, placing exceptional demands on a company’s strategic planning,
management systems, and R&D execution. Leading enterprises in the sector not only
possess multidisciplinary professional teams with deep, long-term expertise in the field
but also leverage sophisticated management structures and digital operation platforms
to achieve highly efficient coordination across R&D processes, supply chain
management, project delivery, and customer service.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS ON OVERSEAS SECURITIES OFFERING AND LISTING

Pursuant to the Trial Administrative Measures of Overseas Securities Offering and
ListingbyDomesticCompanies《( 境內企業境外發行證券和上市管理試行辦法》)promulgated
by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (the “CSRC”) on February 17, 2023, which

carries out securities offering and listing in an overseas market, it shall go through the filing
procedureswiththeCSRCandsubmitrelevantinformation,andshallsubmittheinitialfiling
materials within three working days of submitting the initial public offering and listing
application documents; and (2) PRC companies that are directly or indirectly listing in
overseas markets and intend to conduct subsequent offerings in the same overseas markets
shall go through the filing procedures with the CSRC and report relevant information; they
shall also submit the filing within three working days of the completion date of the
subsequent offering. In addition, no overseas offering and listing shall be conducted under
any of the following circumstances: (1) it is prohibited by the PRC laws, administrative
regulations or relevant rules of the state to conduct overseas offering and listing; (2) overseas
offering and listing may endanger national security as reviewed and determined by the
relevant competent department of the State Council in accordance with the laws; (3) a
domestic enterprise or its controlling shareholder or actual controller has committed a
criminal crime in the last three years; (4) a domestic enterprise is under investigation
according to the laws for being suspected of crimes or major violations of laws and
regulations and no conclusion has yet been made thereof; or (5) there is a major dispute over
ownership of the equity interests held by the controlling shareholder or the shareholder
controlled by the controlling shareholder or the actual controller.

accumulation fund account. The contribution ratio of the housing accumulation fund for
both the employee and the employer may not be lower than 5% of the employee’s monthly
average salary of the previous year; in cities where conditions permit, the contribution ratio
may be appropriately increased.
Regulations in Relation to Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases
ThePreventionandControlof OccupationalDiseasesLawof thePRC《( 中華人民共和
國職業病防治法》), which was promulgated by the SCNPC on October 27, 2001 and latest
amendedonDecember29,2018(the“PreventionandControlof OccupationalDiseasesLaw”),
is the basic law for the prevention and control of occupational diseases. According to the
PreventionandControlof OccupationalDiseasesLaw,budgetforfacilitiesfortheprevention
andcontrolof occupationaldiseasesof aconstructionprojectshallbeincludedinthebudget
of the project and those facilities shall be designed, constructed and put into operation
simultaneously with the main body of the project. The entity that takes charge of the project
should carry out the assessment of the effectiveness of measures for the prevention and
control of occupational diseases before the final acceptance of the construction project. In
addition, employers shall take required administrative measures to prevent and control
occupational diseases in work.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS ON WORK SAFETY
Pursuant to the Work Safety Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國安全生產法》)
promulgated on June 29, 2002, last amended on June 10, 2021 and effective on September 1,
2021, a system of accountability for production safety accidents has been implemented.
Production and business entities must strengthen work safety management, improve work
safety conditions, strengthen standardization and informatization of work safety, and raise
work safety levels. Production and business entities shall meet the work safety conditions
prescribed by such law and other relevant laws, administrative regulations, and national or
industrystandards.Entitiesthatfailtomeetsuchworksafetyconditionsshallnotbeengaged
in production and other business activities. In addition, safety equipment shall be designed,
manufactured, installed, used, tested, maintained, improved, and retired in accordance with
nationalorindustrystandards.Productionandbusinessentitiesshallestablishandimprovea
full-staff work safety responsibility system, clearly defining the responsible person for each
position, the scope of duties, and the evaluation criteria, among others. Production and
business entities shall provide employees with labor protection equipment and work safety
training. Where the primary person-in-charge of a production and business entity fails to
perform his or her duties in respect of work safety, he or she would be subject to legal
liabilities, depending on the seriousness of the relevant work safety accidents.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS IN HONG KONG
The major applicable Hong Kong laws and regulations of Hong Kong which relate to
the business and the subsidiary incorporated in Hong Kong are set out below. This summary
does not purport to be a comprehensive description of all the laws and regulations applicable
to our business in Hong Kong, and/or which may be important to potential investors.
Business Registration Ordinance (Chapter 310 of the Laws of Hong Kong)
Section 5 of the Business Registration Ordinance (Chapter 310 of the Laws of Hong
Kong) requires every person (a company or an individual) carrying on a business in Hong
Kong to register with the Inland Revenue Department and obtain a business registration
certificate within one month of the commencement of the business. Business registration is a
process based on application and does not involve government approval. Once the requisite
criteriaaremet,abusinessregistrationcertificatewillbegranted.Businessregistrationserves
to notify the Inland Revenue Department of the establishment of a business in Hong Kong
and facilitate the collection of tax from businesses in Hong Kong.
Import and Export Ordinance (Chapter 60 of the Laws of Hong Kong)
TheImportandExportOrdinance(Chapter60of theLawsof HongKong)providesfor
the regulation and control of the import of articles into Hong Kong, the export of articles
from Hong Kong, the handling and carriage of articles within Hong Kong which have been
imported into Hong Kong or which may be exported from Hong Kong, and any matter
incidental to or connected with the foregoing. The import and export of certain articles are
prohibited unless with the relevant licences under sections 6C and 6D which are issued under
section 3 of the Import and Export Ordinance (Chapter 60 of the Laws of Hong Kong).

Import and Export (Registration) Regulations (Chapter 60E of the Laws of Hong Kong)
Pursuant to regulations 4 and 5 of the Import and Export (Registration) Regulations,

Inland Revenue Ordinance (Chapter 112 of the Laws of Hong Kong)
The Inland Revenue Ordinance (Chapter 112 of the Laws of Hong Kong) is an

The Inland Revenue Ordinance (Chapter 112 of the Laws of Hong Kong) provides, among
others,thatpersons,whichincludecorporations,partnerships,trusteesandbodiesof persons,

(excludingprofitsarisingfromthesaleof capitalassets)arisinginorderivedfromHongKong
from such trade, profession or business.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN VIETNAM
The principal legislation regulating foreign investment in Vietnam comprises (i) Law
No. 61/2020/QH14 on Investment (the “2020 Law on Investment”), effective from January 1,
2021,(ii)LawNo.143/2025/QH15onInvestment(the“2025LawonInvestment”),effectiveon
March1,2026andreplacingthe2020LawonInvestment,and(iii)LawNo.59/2020/QH14on
Enterprises (the “2020 Law on Enterprises”), effective on January 1, 2021, as amended from
time to time.
AforeigninvestormayinvestinVietnambywayof,amongstothers(i)settingupanew
company; or (ii) contributing capital to or acquiring shares in an existing company. The
general licensing procedures will be comprised of, as the case may be, (i) obtaining capital
acquisition approval; (ii) obtaining/amending an enterprise registration certificate (“ERC”);
and/or(iii)obtaining/amendinganinvestmentregistrationcertificate(“IRC”).Certaincapital
transactionswhichsatisfythethresholdsandcriteriaasprescribedbylawsmayalsobesubject
to the economic concentration review by the competent authorities.
During the course of business, the foreign investor and the foreign-invested company
must strictly follow the contents in the issued IRC and ERC and submit certain periodical
reports relating to the business operation and investment activities. Any changes to the
contentsof thegrantedIRC,ERCandenterpriseregistrationcontentsmustberegisteredwith
or notified to the licensing authorities within the statutory timeline. The amended IRC or
amended ERC or confirmation on changes to enterprise registration contents (where
applicable) will be issued accordingly.
The 2020 Law on Investment and 2025 Law on Investment set out the principles of
investmentprotectionapplicabletoinvestorsdoingbusinessinVietnam.Generally,thelawful
assets of investors shall not be nationalized or confiscated by administrative measures. The
foreign investors are permitted to remit overseas the investment capital, proceeds from
liquidation of investment, income generating from investment activities, and other
lawfully-owned monies and assets after fully discharging financial obligations to the State of
Vietnam in accordance with the laws. In case of change of laws resulting in new investment
incentives, the investors may, as the case may be, be entitled to more favourable incentives
under new regulations or former ones (except for cases relating to national defence and
security, social order and safety, social morals, health of the community or environmental
protection, in which investors will apply for certain measures in consideration for loss of
incentives).

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYMENT IN VIETNAM
The principal statute currently governing employment and labour safety are Labour
CodeNo.45/2019/QH14comingintoeffectonJanuary1,2021andLawNo.84/2015/QH13on
Occupational Safety and Hygiene coming into effect on July 1, 2016.
Labour Contract
Employment relationships are governed by the contractual agreement between
employers and employees. Labour contracts may take one of the following forms: (i)
indefinite-term labour contract; or (ii) definite-term labour contract (the term of which must
not exceed thirty-six months from the effective date of the contract).
A labour contract shall have mandatory contents such as the particulars of employer,
particulars of employees, details of job, employment term, wage/salary, working and resting
time, and social insurance.
A signed labour contract may be terminated under circumstances specified under the
laws. In certain events of termination (such as unilateral termination or dismissal or
termination due to restructuring), the terminating party shall comply with the specific
procedures and conditions required by laws.
Internal Labour Rules (ILRs)
An employer shall promulgate the ILRs which comprise several required contents,
including,interalia,workinghours,occupationalsafetyandhygiene,protectionof assetsand
intellectual properties and labour discipline. The ILRs must be notified to the employees and
its main contents must be posted at essential locations in the workplace.
If the employer has at least 10 employees or more, it shall register the ILRs with the
local labour authority at the province where the employer is located.
Foreign Employees
Foreigners who work in Vietnam are required to obtain from the local labour authority
aworkpermitoraconfirmation/notificationthattheyareexemptedfromworkpermitsbefore
starting to work. The term of a work permit shall not exceed two years. The term of labour
contract of a foreigner working in Vietnam must not exceed the term of the work permit.
Statutory Insurance
Employers and employees shall contribute compulsory insurance at respective rates
based on salary, as stipulated under the Vietnam laws and regulations, to the social insurance
fund on a monthly basis.
Labour safety and hygiene
Employers and employees are subject to various requirements on labour safety and
hygiene at the workplace such as periodical testing of machinery, equipment and materials
with strict requirements on labour safety; personal protective facilities; and periodic health
checks.
– 98 –

=== PAGE 108 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO TAXATION IN VIETNAM
A foreign-invested company in Vietnam is mainly subject to the following taxes:
Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
EnterprisesestablishedunderVietnamlawsaresubjecttocorporateincometaxwiththe
standard corporate income tax rate being 20%. However, preferential tax rates, tax
exemptionsortaxreductionsmaybeavailabletoeligibleprojectsincertainindustriesthatare
encouraged by the Vietnamese government (e.g. scientific research and technological
development, construction investment and business of high-tech incubator, high-tech
enterprise incubator) or preferential investment locations (i.e. poor and remote areas).
Personal Income Tax (PIT)
Companies are not subject to PIT. However, as income-paying entities, companies will,
for and on behalf of employees, declare, withhold and pay the PIT imposed on income, that
companies pay to employees, to the State Budget monthly or quarterly. In addition, the
companies will conduct PIT finalization of all types of tax income paid to the employees by
the end of tax period upon authorization by employees.
Value-Added Tax (VAT)
Goods and services used for manufacturing, business and consumption in Vietnam are
subject to VAT, except for several goods and services, inter alia, software, certain financial,
insuranceandbankingservices,andmedicalhealthservicesandveterinaryservices.Different
standard VAT rates, including 10%, 5% and 0%, are applied subject to the types of goods and
services.Taxincentivesmaybeavailablesubjecttothepoliciesof theVietnamesegovernment
from time to time.
Import Tax and Export Tax
Import tax or export tax imposes on goods imported or exported across the borders of
Vietnam, or which pass between the domestic market and a non-tariff zone in Vietnam, with
certain exemptions such as goods in transit and goods given as humanitarian aid and
non-refundable aid. The different tax rates are applied subject to the type of imported or
exported goods.
Foreign Withholding Contractor Tax (FWCT)
FWCT applies to certain payments to foreign parties including interest, royalties,
servicefees,lease,insurance,transportation,transfersof securitiesandgoodssuppliedwithin
Vietnam or associated with services rendered in Vietnam, and certain distribution
arrangements. FWCT comprises a combination of CIT (or PIT in case of payment to foreign
individuals) and VAT at varying rates subject to specific types of goods supplied and service
rendered.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO FOREIGN EXCHANGE CONTROL IN
VIETNAM
A company incorporated under the laws of Vietnam is designated as a “resident” for
exchange control purposes in Vietnam. This includes foreign-invested enterprises.
– 99 –

=== PAGE 109 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Foreign Currency Payment
Foreign currency payments within the territory of Vietnam are strictly prohibited for
mostof transactionsbetweenVietnameseresidentsandaresubjecttothestrictcontrolof the
State Bank of Vietnam. The law provides for certain exceptions such as: (i) resident
organizations may internally transfer capital in foreign currencies via bank transfer (as
between an entity with legal status and a ‘dependent accounting entity’ or vice versa); (ii)
residentsmaycontributecapitalinforeigncurrenciesviabanktransfersinordertoimplement
foreign investment projects in Vietnam; and/or (iii) residents are entitled to receive payments
in foreign currencies made via bank transfers in accordance with import or export contracts;
(iv) residents that are export processing enterprises may quote, price, and settle payments in
foreign currencies via bank transfer for certain processing and export-related transactions.
Foreign Currency Conversion and Remittance
A resident company incorporated under the laws of Vietnam is allowed to remit
overseas foreign currency to meet its payment requirements for permitted transactions with
non-residents, subject to applicable Vietnam laws and the bank’s verification. Certain
permitted transactions include (i) payments and remittance in relation to import and export
of goods and services; (ii) payments and remittance in relation to revenues from direct and
indirect investment; (iii) payments for principal and interest under foreign loans; and/or (iv)
other payments and transfers as prescribed by the State Bank of Vietnam.
Direct Investment Capital Account
Aresidentforeign-investedcompanyshallopenadirectinvestmentcapitalaccount(the
“DICA”), in foreign currency which foreign investor selects to contribute capital to the
company,atalicensedbankinVietnam.Certaintransactionsandpaymentsarerequiredtobe
made via the DICA, inter alia, (i) receipt of charter capital contributions; (ii) disbursement
outside Vietnam of capital, profit and other lawful income of a foreign investor; (iii)
disbursementandrepaymentof foreignloansinthesamecurrencyof DICA;and/or(iv)other
revenue and disbursement transactions relating to direct foreign investment activities.
Repatriation of Dividends
Foreign investors may remit overseas the profits from foreign-invested company via
DICA once such foreign-invested company has been profitable and has discharged all its
financial obligations towards the Government of Vietnam and completed statutory
procedures. A notification on overseas remittance of profits must be submitted to the
competent tax authority before the offshore repatriation of dividends is made.
There are no withholding taxes or remittance taxes imposed on dividends paid to the
foreign corporate investors or owners of the foreign-invested companies.
Offshore Loans
Loans granted by foreign lenders to Vietnamese entities, including foreign-invested
companies, are permitted upon satisfaction of relevant conditions and, if application,
completion of the procedural registration. Loans provided by offshore lenders with a term of
morethan12monthsmustberegisteredwiththeStateBankof Vietnam.Offshoreloansshall
be disbursed and repaid via a proper bank account such as DICA as the case may be.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS IN
VIETNAM
Copyright
Copyright comprises moral rights and economic rights. Authors who use their own
time, finance and material or technical facilities to create works shall have the moral rights
andtheeconomicrightsunderthelaws.Certainof suchmoralrightsandeconomicrightsmay
alsobevestedinanorganizationwhichassignsitsstaff orengagesanauthortocreateawork,
unless otherwise agreed.
Literary, artistic and scientific works are covered by copyright, including, among
others, computer programs, data collections, books, music, paintings, and others. No
copyright registration is compulsory in Vietnam.
Trademark, Patent and Industrial Design
Registration of trademark, patent or industrial design is not compulsory under laws of
Vietnam. An organization may register for protecting its (i) patent and industrial designs the
creationof whichisfundedbysuchorganizationintheformof jobassignmentorengagement
with authors (unless otherwise legally agreed) and (ii) trademarks in relation to the products
produced or services provided by such organization, from unlawful usage by third parties.
A certificate of registered trademark shall be valid from the grant date until the end of
ten years from the filing date, and may be renewed for many consecutive terms, each of ten
years.Aninventionpatentshallbevalidfromthegrantdateuntiltheendof twentyyearsafter
the filing date. An industrial design patent shall be valid from the grant date until the end of
five years from the filing date, and may be renewed for two consecutive terms, each of five
years.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN
VIETNAM
The principal statute currently governing environmental matters is Law No.
72/2020/QH14onEnvironmentalProtectionwhichhascomeintoeffectsinceJanuary1,2022,
as amended from time to time.
Theinvestorsand/ortheinvesteecompaniesarerequiredtocomplywithenvironmental
protection obligations, including, among others: (i) carrying out licensing procedures for
environmental impact assessment, environmental permits, and/or environmental registration
before commencing the investment project; and (ii) during the operation of the investment
project, applying appropriate measures to protect the environment, such as collecting,
classifying, storing, and/or treating waste, and ensuring sufficient human resources and
equipment to prevent or respond to environmental incidents, in accordance with Vietnamese
laws.

OVERVIEW
Our Company was incorporated under the name of Dalian Dongfang Kemai
Electronics Co., Ltd. (大連東方科脈電子有限公司) in the PRC on October 28, 2005 as a
limited liability company with a registered capital of RMB10,000,000.
On December 11, 2015, our Company was converted into a joint stock company with
limited liability.
We are a prominent player in the global e-paper display industry. We were the second
largestglobale-paperdisplaymanufacturerbyrevenuein2025,withamarketshareof 20.8%,
and the largest global commercial e-paper display manufacturer by revenue, with a market
share of 24.9%, according to CIC. The global commercial e-paper display segment accounted
for 83.5% of the overall global e-paper display market in 2025 in terms of revenue,
underscoring our market position in the industry.

PUBLIC FLOAT
Based on an Offer Price of HK$78.64, HK$89.88 and HK$101.11 per H Share, being
the low-end, mid-point and high-end of the Offer Price range respectively, the minimum
public float percentage threshold under Rule 19A.13A(1) is 25%, 25% and 25% respectively.
Upon completion of the Global Offering (assuming that the Over-allotment Option is

shares for which listing is sought that are held by the public and not subject to any disposal
restrictions (whether under contract, the Listing Rules, applicable laws or otherwise), at the
time of listing, must: (a) represent at least 10% of the total number of issued shares in the
class to which H shares belong at the time of listing (excluding treasury shares), with an
expected market value at the time of listing of not less than HK$50,000,000; or (b) have an
expected market value at the time of listing of not less than HK$600,000,000.
Our Company will comply with the free float requirement under Rule 19A.13C of the
Listing Rules at the time of Listing.

PREVIOUS LISTING APPLICATION
On June 30, 2023, our Company submitted an application (the “A Share Listing
Application”) for listing (the “A Share Listing”) of our Shares on the main board of the
Shanghai Stock Exchange. The Shanghai Stock Exchange issued two rounds of comments
while reviewing the A Share Listing Application, to which our Company provided responses.
In view of (i) our business development and strategic planning considerations; and (ii)
thethenlistingqualificationsapplicabletous,andafterathoroughanalysisof theprevailing
capital market conditions and other relevant factors, we decided to withdraw the A Share
Listing Application and the plan for the A Share Listing. There is no material outstanding
comments in relation to the A Share Listing Application prior to such withdrawal.
On May 10, 2024, we applied for withdrawal of the A Shares Listing Application, and
the Shanghai Stock Exchange has accepted such withdrawal application and issued the
Decision in relation to the Termination of the Review of the Initial Public Offering and
Listingof DKEHoldingCompanyLimitedontheMainBoard《( 關於終止對浙江東方科脈電
子股份有限公司首次公開發行股票並在主板上市審核的決定》) on May 20, 2024. We had
addressedallcommentsraisedbytheShanghaiStockExchange,andnoadditionalcomments
werereceivedfromthem,uptothedateof thewithdrawalof theAShareListingApplication.
The withdrawal of the A Share Listing was not attributable to any issues related to the
operations of our Company or our Controlling Shareholders.
Considering that the Stock Exchange would provide our Company with an
internationalplatformtoaccessforeigncapital,attractdiverseoverseasinvestorsandincrease
ourinternationalexposure,allof whichbeingbeneficialtoourexpansiontotheinternational
market, our Company decided to pursue a Listing of the H Shares on the Stock Exchange in
ordertoprovidefurthercapitalforourR&Dandgeneralworkingcapitalasdescribedinmore
details in “Future Plans and Use of Proceeds.”
To the best of our Directors’knowledge, information and belief, our Directors are not

to the attention of the Stock Exchange or the Shareholders.
