BUSINESS
OVERVIEW
We are a prominent player in the global e-paper display industry. We were the second
largestglobale-paperdisplaymanufacturerbyrevenuein2025,withamarketshareof 20.8%,
and the largest global commercial e-paper display manufacturer by revenue, with a market
share of 24.9%, according to CIC. The global commercial e-paper display segment accounted
for 83.5% of the overall global e-paper display market in 2025 in terms of revenue,
underscoring our market position in the industry.
Overthepast15years,wehaveaccumulatedexperienceine-paperdisplayindustryand
built capabilities in proprietary design and manufacturing of e-paper display modules. We
focus on the R&D, production and sales of a wide range of e-paper display modules covering
afullspectrumof displaycolorsandsizes.Ourproductportfolioisusedindiverseapplication
scenarios including smart retail, smart offices, smart education, smart logistics, smart
transportation, e-readers and emerging applications.
We have built a presence in the global e-paper display industry through sustained
research and development. Our success is reflected in a series of key milestones as set forth
below:
• Wecommencedourbusinessin2005,initiallyfocusingonthedesignandR&Dof
industrial-grade LCD monitors and display modules. Drawing from our
experience in display technology, we had at the time recognized the significant
potential of e-paper in the development of IoT applications. In 2008, we
establishedoure-paperR&Dteam,becomingoneof theearliestcompaniesinthe
PRC to enter the e-paper display industry;
• In 2010, we signed a joint development agreement with E Ink Corporation, a
subsidiary of E Ink Holdings, which is a global leader in e-paper display
technology, covering joint R&D and accelerating innovation. In 2018, E Ink
Holdings further reinforced this partnership through a strategic equity
investment in us through its wholly-owned subsidiary;
• By 2018, we had completed a full strategic transformation into e-paper display,
supportedbyourtwomanufacturingbasesinDalianandJiaxingComprehensive
Bonded Zone, enabling rapid product upgrades and capacity expansion;
• In 2021, we launched the construction of our Jiaxing headquarters production
base which commenced full operation in 2023 and was, according to CIC, the
world’s largest e-paper display module production base as of the Latest
Practicable Date in terms of both gross floor area and number of production
lines. In 2023, our first fully automated e-paper module production line also
commenced mass production, significantly enhancing efficiency, quality, and
traceability. By December 31, 2025, our annual production capacity for e-paper
display modules was around 160 million units across 50 specialized production
lines;
• In2023,webecamethefirstprovidergloballytodeploye-paperdisplayproducts
applied in the field of intelligent robotics;
• In2024,wecommencedconstructionof ourfirstoverseasmanufacturingfacility
in Vietnam, while also launching the world’s first OTFT-based flexible e-paper
display with 180° bending capability according to CIC. We were also the first
manufacturer globally to achieve mass production of a curved e-paper
touchscreen hardware wallet using OTFT technology. This product earned us the
2025 ePaper Industry Alliance Pioneering Award for e-paper technological
innovation;
– 125 –

=== PAGE 135 ===
BUSINESS
• In2025,ourfirstoverseasproductionbase,theVietnammanufacturingbase,was
completed and officially commenced production, making us one of the few
companies in the global e-paper display industry with self-built overseas
manufacturing capacity. Simultaneously, we completed the development of
large-size e-paper products based on the E6 full-color display series, taking the
lead in the industrial mass production and application of fast-refresh color
e-paper display modules, demonstrating our pursuit of technological
advancement. Our 13.3-inch full-color e-paper display module was awarded the
2025 “IOTE Gold Award”by the Shenzhen IoT Industry Association.
As a prominent player in the global e-paper display industry, we continuously pursue
R&D and innovation to strengthen our core competitiveness. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, we held 98 patents, including 32 invention patents, solidifying the technology
capabilities to support the expansion of our product portfolio. Going forward, we will
continue to invest in the R&D of new and enhanced products such as flexible, full-color and
ultra-large displays, further enriching our offerings and delivering more advanced,
high-quality products for our customers and the industry.
Toefficientlyserveourglobalcustomers,wehaveestablishedfourproductionandR&D
bases,beingthelargestnumberamongindustryplayersworldwideasof theLatestPracticable
Date according to CIC, together with multiple offices across China and overseas, which
provide comprehensive customer service targeting markets in Europe, America, Asia, among
others. Leveraging our localized presence, we continuously optimize supply chain and
logistics costs for our customers, ensuring an agile and reliable response to their needs.
Buildingonyearsof industryexperienceandbusinesscapabilities,wehavecontinuedto
deliver steady progress in both scale and operational efficiency. Sales of our e-paper display
modules increased from 56.1 million units in 2023 to 67.1 million units in 2024 and further to
124.5 million units in 2025. During the Track Record Period, we maintained substantial
investment in R&D, achieving a CAGR of 21.6% in R&D spending from 2023 to 2025. In
2023, 2024 and 2025, our revenue was RMB1,024.2 million, RMB1,151.6 million and
RMB1,713.0 million, respectively, and our profit for the year was RMB50.7 million,
RMB53.4 million and RMB80.2 million, respectively.
We have launched new e-paper display products, including full-color, large-size
billboard products. Our product pipeline also includes small- and medium-sized full-color
OTFT, PI a-Si and other flexible products, full-color, large-size products powered by Spectra
6 technology, as well as multi-color, wide-temperature products powered by Spectra 3100
technology. With these innovations, our application scenarios are extending beyond smart
retail into smart office, smart education, smart logistics, smart transportation and smart
healthcare, unlocking significant revenue growth potential.
OUR STRENGTHS
We believe the following competitive strengths contribute to our success:
An early industry entrant with established production scale and deep-rooted customer
relationships
According to CIC, we were one of the earliest companies in the PRC to enter the
e-paperdisplayindustryandhavebuiltareputablepositionovertheyears.In2025,weranked
first globally among commercial e-paper display manufacturers in terms of revenue, with a
market share of 24.9%.
As of December 31, 2025, we had established four production bases in Jiaxing and
Dalian,ChinaandPhuThoProvince,Vietnam,operatingatotalof 50specializedproduction
lines. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had the most number of production bases in the
global e-paper display industry according to CIC. Our sales and service networks extend to
numerous countries and regions worldwide.

BUSINESS
The trust of globally recognized clients strengthens our industry position. We have
successfully established a presence in the supply chains of numerous international brands in

partnerships with the world’s top e-paper application providers. Leveraging flexible
customization capabilities, reliable delivery, consistent product quality and comprehensive
after-sales support, we deliver advanced e-paper display modules to customers, successfully
serving these top global e-paper application providers.
These high-quality customer resources not only generate recurring business orders but
also provide valuable market insights and opportunities for technological collaboration. We
have established an in-depth collaboration mechanism with the top global providers of
e-paper application. Through shared demand forecasts, customized solution development,
andjointmarketexpansion,wecaneffectivelyimproveourresponsivenesstocustomerservice
and strengthen our market share.
Stable, mutually beneficial and collaborative supply chain system
Weserveasavice-chairingmemberof theElectronicPaperIndustryAlliance.Suchrole
not only reflects our industry position but also enhance our influence in setting industry
standards and promoting collaborative innovation. We have established long-standing
partnerships with suppliers of core raw materials, including e-ink film, TFT substrates and
driver ICs. Through strategic cooperation agreements and capacity supply agreements, we
have established a resilient and diversified supply chain. This foundation ensures consistent
productquality,reducessupplychainrisks,andenablesustorespondeffectivelytolarge-scale
and fast-changing market demands.
Furthermore, we are collaborating with key raw material suppliers to jointly develop
new products and applications, fostering the mode of cooperation utilizing complementary
strengthsandsharedresources.Thiswellpositionsusforindustryadvanceswhileenablingus
to deliver reliable, high-performance e-paper display products to our downstream customers.
By driving continuous innovation in e-paper technology and accelerating its adoption across
global IoT devices, we aim to create shared value along the supply chain and steadily expand
our global footprint.
Strong technical expertise and continuous innovation as core drivers
With over 15 years of expertise in e-paper display industry, we have built a solid
foundationof coreknow-howandadvancedmanufacturingprocesses.Ourinnovativee-paper
intelligent cutting and layout system has successfully overcome common challenges in the
e-paper display industry. By optimizing cutting techniques and intelligent layout algorithms,
we have enhanced the utilization rate of medium- and large-sized e-ink films. This
breakthrough, which has been granted a national utility patent, pioneers a brand new
cost-reduction pathway for global e-paper display manufacturers. Additionally, we are the
first in the industry to introduce FPL master sheet inspection system, effectively boosting
master film inspection efficiency and production yield.
In terms of full-color, we have developed full-color e-paper modules that offer faster
refresh rates, higher resolution, a wider color gamut, and richer saturation. In terms of
flexibility, we have successfully achieved large-scale mass production application of OTFT
technology in e-paper products, and achieved the world’s first mass production of
OTFT-basedflexiblee-paperproductsaccordingtoCIC.Intermsof segmentcodeandprism,
we draw on years of accumulated expertise to support a full product range from small to
medium and large sizes.
We adopt an R&D model that prioritizes “in-house innovation,” supplemented by
“open collaboration.” In terms of in-house innovation, we strengthen the technological
capabilities to accelerate the industrialization of full-color e-paper (E Ink Spectra 6) and
flexible e-paper. In terms of open collaboration, we partner with leading universities on joint
projects aimed at improving backplane and substrate performance. We are also actively
developing a patent portfolio across various areas, including driver design and flexible
packaging, with dozens of patents already granted.

BUSINESS
WeremainfirmlycommittedtoR&Dinvestment,keepingpacewithkeyindustrytrends

Exceptional large-scale production capabilities and highly automated intelligent manufacturing
We were the second largest global e-paper display manufacturer by revenue in 2025,
withamarketshareof 20.8%,andthelargestglobalcommerciale-paperdisplaymanufacturer
by revenue, with a market share of 24.9%, according to CIC. The global commercial e-paper
display segment accounted for 83.5% of the overall global e-paper display market in 2025 in
terms of revenue, underscoring our market position in the industry.
Our large-scale operations allow us to spread fixed costs more efficiently and unlock
significant economies of scale across raw material sourcing, manufacturing, and operations.
Our continued investment in production has enabled us to rapidly expand our production
capacity,increasingourproductioncapacityof e-paperdisplaymodulesfrom89millionunits
in 2023 to 160 million units in 2025. Our scale advantage, coupled with highly efficient
operations,enablesustomaintainstrongcostcompetitivenesswhileensuringproductquality,
delivering cost-effective products to customers.
We continuously improve production efficiency and product yield through intelligent
production lines and well-established process systems. Given the sensitivity of core e-paper
materialstoenvironmentaltemperatureandhumidity,wehavebuiltanenvironmentalcontrol
system spanning the entire value chain from raw material transportation, storage and
production. We partner with specialized equipment providers to develop tailored production
modules and integrate them with our proprietary assembly processes and system tuning
technologies.Thisdeeplyintegratedandcustomizedsetuphascreatedanintelligentassembly
line that is difficult to replicate, making it challenging for competitors to build a production
systemof comparablescaleandprecisionintheshortterm.OurClass1,000andClass10,000
cleanrooms provide stringent particle control. We monitor and automatically adjust
temperature and humidity in real time, while also deploying energy-saving systems to reduce

BUSINESS
Each e-paper display module is a fully integrated display assembly comprising key
components such as e-ink film (an FPL), TFT substrate, driver IC, protective film, and FPC.
As the core component of e-paper display screens, e-paper display modules deliver essential
functionality in a range of smart, low-power display applications. Below sets forth an
illustration of the structure of e-paper display module:
RTV

Prior to room-temperature After RTV adhesive

Within each module, the function of each key component is set out below:
Key Component Description
FPC . . . . . . . . . . . . . Flexible printed circuit, a flexible circuit board used in
e-paper display modules to connect the display panel with
driver circuits, allowing bendable or compact wiring
designs
Driver IC . . . . . . . . . An integrated circuit that controls the operation of an
e-paper display module, manages pixel activation, signal
timing and data processing
TFT . . . . . . . . . . . . . Thin film transistor, a semiconductor device made by
depositing thin layers of materials on a substrate,
commonly used to precisely control pixels in display
technologies
FPL . . . . . . . . . . . . . Front plane laminate, the topmost layer of an e-paper display
module. It directly determines the display performance
Protective film . . . . . a functional film mainly made of polystyrene which provides
anti-glare performance, high-level moisture barrier (to
prevent e-ink from dampness), and UV blocking capability,
thereby extending the lifespan of e-paper modules
EC Adhesive. . . . . . . EC adhesive is used to firmly bond key components in an
e-paper display module such as the e-ink film, conductive
layer, protective glass, or plastic substrate together to
ensure structural stability
RTV Adhesive . . . . . Room-Temperature Vulcanizing silicone adhesive is primarily
applied to provide sealing, cushioning and electrical
insulation within the e-paper display module, ensuring
structural integrity and environmental protection
Silver Paste. . . . . . . . Silver paste is applied to establish electrical interconnection
between the flexible circuit and the e-paper display module
layer
ACF. . . . . . . . . . . . . Anisotropic conductive film, primarily applied to achieve
electrical interconnection and mechanical bonding between
circuit components within the e-paper display module,
ensuring high precision and reliability

BUSINESS
Assembly of each module involves two key steps, namely: (A) FOG ACF, the
flex-on-glass process which utilizes ACF to establish electrical interconnection and
mechanical bonding between the flexible printed circuit and the glass substrate within the
e-paper display module, and (B) COG ACF, the chip-on-glass process which utilizes ACF to
achieveelectricalinterconnectionandmechanicalbondingbetweenthedriverICandtheglass
substrate within the e-paper display module.
Our e-paper display module constitutes the hardware set of an e-paper display
end-product, and it functions as a key component that converts data into image signals for
display on e-paper, ultimately driving the operation of the e-paper display end-product. Our
production process entails the cutting, lamination, bonding and dispensing of various raw
materials to assemble the final e-paper display modules which utilizes core e-paper display
technologiesownedbythird-partysuppliersmainlywithrespecttorawmaterialssuchase-ink
films. In the overall e-paper display value chain, our e-paper display module can be viewed as
a semi-finished product as it needs to be integrated into the e-paper display end-product to
deliver its full functionality. The e-paper display end-product may take different forms
depending on its downstream applications.
Our product specifications meet the diversified needs of mainstream application
scenarios. Leveraging our proprietary driving waveform architecture and extensive
accumulated tuning data, our products outperform industry averages in key display
performance indicators such as clarity and contrast. In particular, our products’ optical
performance metrics (LAB values) for white and yellow surpass the recommended standards
proposed by E Ink Holdings. Through self-developed inspection technologies and
comprehensive temperature and humidity control throughout the production process, we
ensure product consistency and stability. In addition, our fully automated production lines
enable high yield rates and significant cost advantages.

Capability to adapt to product iteration and expand downstream applications

incorporated into both our existing and new products, ensuring the continuous advancement
of our technological competitiveness.

OUR TECHNOLOGIES AND RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
WeadoptaR&Dmodelthatprioritizes“in-houseinnovation,”supplementedby“open
collaboration.” In terms of in-house innovation, we strengthen technological capabilities to
acceleratetheindustrializationof full-colore-paper(EInkSpectra6)andflexiblee-paper.In
terms of open collaboration, we partner with leading universities on joint projects aimed at
improvingbackplaneandsubstrateperformance.Weindependentlyowncoretechnologiesfor
the design and manufacturing of e-paper display modules.
As of December 31, 2025, our R&D team consisted of 207 dedicated talents,
approximately 5.8% of whom held a master’s degree or above. In particular, our R&D team is
headed by Dr. Chun-Kang Ku, who holds a Ph.D. in chemical engineering with nearly two
decades of experience in the semiconductor and new materials industries, and having worked
at TSMC, Taiwan’s Industrial Technology Research Institute and Rudolph Technologies
coveringbothreputableR&Dinstitutionandmultinationalcorporations.Fortheyearsended
December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we recorded R&D expenses of RMB39.9 million,

revenue, respectively.
Our Core Technologies
Our proprietary core technologies cover both product feature technologies and
manufacturing and assembly technologies.
Product features technologies mainly include: (a) color e-paper display module
technology which delivers high color saturation and brightness and achieves a refresh rate
comparabletothatof black-and-whitee-inkdisplays,meetingtheapplicationrequirementsof
advanced products such as color e-book readers; (b) flexible e-paper display module
technology where we have strong design and manufacturing processes for flexible e-paper
display modules, with core technologies mastered particularly in the R&D and design of 3D
curved screens, including curved lamination, sealing processes, and transfer handling
platforms for flexible substrates; and (c) e-paper display module waveform optimization
technology where we have enhanced display performance by utilizing waveform tuning
technology, tailored to the material characteristics of different e-paper display modules and
their specific application scenarios.
Manufacturing and assembly technologies mainly include: (a) e-ink film cutting
technology where we have independently developed specialized jigs for the laser cutting of
e-ink films, which address issues such as light reflection, airflow interference, and edge
melting. Paired with an intelligent layout system, we optimize cutting patterns and enhance
material utilization; (b) e-paper display module lamination, edge encapsulation, bubble
removal and curing technologies where we collaborated with equipment manufacturers to
develop high-precision, lamination platforms integrating automatic misalignment detection
and intelligent monitoring, together with automated dispensing and programmable
de-bubblingequipment;and(c)e-paperdisplaymoduletestingtechnologywhereweoptimize
testing processes by leveraging the paper-like characteristics of e-paper through pre-driving
the device to test images. We have independently developed testing fixtures with
auto-activation functionality and collaborated with equipment suppliers to create a
circular-trackAutomatedOpticalInspection(AOI)solution,effectivelyshorteningthetesting
cycle while improving detection efficiency and defect capture rates.

Cooperative R&D
To advance collaborative innovation, we develop cooperative relationships with (i)
businesspartners,(ii)researchinstitutionsanduniversitiesand(iii)governmentalagencies.In
terms of university-enterprise collaboration, we have launched joint R&D projects with
Chineseleadinguniversitiesontheapplicationresearchof flexibleintegratedcircuits.Wealso
undertook the Liaoning Province Challenge & Leadership Science and Technology Program
toconductR&Donthedevelopmentandapplicationof novelthree-dimensionalcolormixing
display technologies. During the Track Record Period, we carried out a total of 106 R&D
projects, comprising 101 in-house R&D projects and five collaborative R&D projects. We
engaged five external partners for these collaborative R&D initiatives.
The salient terms of our collaboration with external R&D partners are set forth below:
Scopeof collaboration.Theagreementsspecifytheresearchpurposeof theprojectsand
the specific obligations of each party.
IPownership.ThepartiestypicallyjointlyownanyIPrightsdevelopedinthejointR&D
under the agreements. IP rights that arise prior to the agreement or independent from the
other party belong to their original owners.
Roles and responsibilities. We are responsible for the provision of (i) necessary research
materials,(ii)technicalsupport,and(iii)accesstoourR&DCenter.Theexternalpartnersare
responsible for (i) planning and designing research project, (ii) delivery research results and
(iii) coordination of laboratory usage. Both parties collaborate to support the promotion of
R&D and contribute to the development of new IPs.
Confidentiality. The parties are responsible for maintaining strict confidentiality of all
confidential information provided by the other parties.
Termination. The agreements can be terminated upon failure to achieve project
objectives with all parties’consent, and the parties shall bear their own losses.
We maintain collaborative relationships with key raw material suppliers, such as E Ink
Holdings, as we rely on raw material suppliers to provide the essential materials required for
ourR&Dprojectsandproductionprocesses.DuringtheR&Dprocess,weworkwithsuppliers
on material selection and solution design, and in some cases entrust them with customized
material development. We also conduct upstream material research and collaborate with one
of our suppliers to develop flexible e-paper technology. In addition, we have signed an
exclusive global licensing agreement for OTFT technology in the field of e-paper with this
supplier (the “OTFT Licensing Agreement”), which expands its application in high-end
scenarios. By cultivating these partnerships, we are able to share resources, co-develop
technologies and strengthen the ecosystem for e-paper display products.

PRODUCTION
Our production process ensures high standards of quality control while maintaining
flexibility and efficiency, enabling us to respond quickly and effectively to diverse customer
demands. Leveraging advanced design and manufacturing capabilities, we actively drive the
industrialization of e-paper display products, enabling broad applications in the smart IoT
sector and supporting the intelligent transformation of industries.
We leverage our advanced manufacturing facilities in Jiaxing, Dalian, and Vietnam —
equipped with automated SMT lines, precision assembly systems, AOI vision inspection, and
fullyintegratedMES—tocontrolkeyprocessesincludingPCBassembly,moduleintegration,
and quality testing. This highly automated, data-driven approach enables strict quality
control, protection of intellectual property, rapid responsiveness, and scalable production,
supporting our industry position in the e-paper display market while ensuring compliance
with international standards. For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, the
number of failures per million, or PPM, for our products showed a consistent and significant
improvement, declining from 992 to 499, and ultimately to 447. This sustained downward
trend reflects the effectiveness of our robust quality control systems and continuous process
optimization.AchievingsuchlowPPMlevelsunderscoresthereliabilityanddurabilityof our
products and reaffirms our commitment to delivering superior quality to customers.
Furthermore, during the Track Record Period, we maintained a customer acceptance rate of
99.9%, further evidencing the high quality and performance of our products.

BUSINESS
Production Process
We primarily adopt an order-driven production model, under which production is
generally scheduled based on customer orders while taking into account product
specifications, delivery timelines and current production capacity. Our production planning
department formulates the production plan based on order information provided by the sales
department. Once approved, the plan is carried out by the manufacturing team.
We are committed to improving our production processes, enhancing manufacturing
and management capabilities, and advancing the automation and digitalization of our
production lines to build a more efficient and intelligent manufacturing system. The
production cycle starts when a batch of products is scheduled based on a purchase order and
ends when the finished goods are warehoused. Subject to product specification, the complete
manufacturing cycle for E4 product and “Black & White + Low Temperature” product is
generally between two and three weeks, the complete manufacturing cycle for E5 product is
generally between three to four weeks.
We have developed a robust and scalable production system that supports the efficient
manufacturing of e-paper display modules. Our production process mainly consists of three
keystages,namelyrawmaterialcutting,laminationandbonding,andadhesivedispensingand
inspection.
Below sets forth highlights in the three major steps in our production process.

Raw material cutting. We precisely cut the purchased TFT glass, e-ink film, and
protective films according to the product specifications, effectively mitigating issues such as
light reflection, bubble residue, edge melting, and improving edge sintering and damage.
Lamination and Bonding. We enhance the alignment accuracy of e-paper display
modules through key lamination and bonding processes, including silver paste dispensing,
e-ink film lamination, COG bonding, FOG bonding, and protective film lamination,
effectively improving product yield and reliability.
Adhesive dispensing and Inspection. We first conduct an initial inspection of the
semi-finished products, followed by a series of adhesive dispensing and inspection including
edge sealing, defoaming and curing, RTV dispensing and OTP Programming, followed by
final inspection to enhance display quality and production efficiency.
Intelligent and Automated Production
Wehaveestablishedahighlyautomated,intelligent,andscalablemanufacturingsystem
that ensures high efficiency, superior product quality, and rapid responsiveness for our
operations.
Automated Production Network
We incorporated automated production lines into our production processes to handle
highlyrepetitiveandcomplextasks,whichreduceshumanerrorandenhancesthequalityand
consistencyof ourproducts.Wehaveestablishedasystematiclayoutof automatedproduction
lines across our four production bases in Jiaxing headquarters, Jiaxing Comprehensive
Bonded Zone, Dalian, and Phu Tho in Vietnam, forming a comprehensive and highly capable
smart manufacturing network.

BUSINESS
This strategic footprint contributes to steady and responsive production for different
market segments.
MES System
We are actively advancing the implementation and upgrading of our Manufacturing
Execution System (MES), progressively achieving greater visibility, full traceability, and
intelligent decision-making in production processes. Currently, the MES system has been
successfully deployed in lines at the Jiaxing Comprehensive Bonded Zone base and Jiaxing
headquarters base. Full deployment at Dalian and Vietnam bases is planned as of the Latest
Practicable Date for completion by 2026. Core system functionalities include unit-level
product tracking, full production history traceability, output and yield reporting (based on
customized report development), material management (including material usage control,
feeder verification, and shelf-life validation), equipment inspections, and digitalized quality
inspection and sampling. Through integration of the MES system, our Company has
significantly reduced human errors, enhanced production transparency and management
efficiency, and effectively driven the transformation of its production model from
“experience-driven”to “data-driven.”
AOI Vision Inspection System
We have implemented an Automated Optical Inspection (“AOI”) vision inspection
system that covers the inspection processes for FPL motherboards, semi-finished goods, and
finished products. The system significantly improves inspection efficiency of product quality,
reducesfalsepositives,andensuresconsistentproductquality.Ourcustomeracceptancerates
consistently outperform industry averages according to CIC. To further strengthen quality
management, we have established a rigorous quality control system and have obtained
international certifications including ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, and ISO 14067,
demonstrating our systematic and standardized approach to quality, environmental
management, occupational health and safety, and carbon footprint management.
QUALITY CONTROL
Product Quality and Safety
We operate a unified production management system covering material use, process
control, and quality assurance to ensure consistent product quality. Since the core raw
materials are sensitive to temperature and humidity, we have implemented an environmental
control system across transportation, storage, and production, supported by Class 1,000 and
Class 10,000 cleanrooms. We have adopted energy-efficient measures and photovoltaic
systemsatourproductionfacilitiestopromotegreenmanufacturing.Ourproductionlinesare
highly automated, reducing labor costs, improving efficiency, and enhancing quality
consistency.
WealsomaintaininternalqualitycontrolsystemsthatcomplywithISO9001:2015,and
our products meet customer requirements. During the Track Record Period and up to the
Latest Practicable Date, we did not record any material accidents or injuries arising from our
production processes or the use of our products.
Product Returns and Warranty
The warranty for our products varies by product type. We maintain active post-sales
communication and work closely with customers to address any quality issues. We have
established a standardized process for handling customer complaints and returns, supported
by a feedback mechanism on product quality. For defects attributable to us, we perform
root-cause analyses, issue 8D reports, and inspect, repair, or replace returned items. These
measures enable us to maintain customer satisfaction and continuously improve product
quality.

BUSINESS
PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLIERS
Raw Materials and Procurement
We have established a standardized and efficient procurement management system that
ensures stable raw material supply and supports our production operations. Distinct
procurement processes are in place for raw materials, production-related assets, and office
assets, covering order management, procurement planning, supplier management and
qualification review, and procurement execution, with all procedures maintained in a
compliant, transparent, and traceable manner.
Our principal raw materials include e-ink films, TFT substrates, driver ICs, protective
films, FPCs and other related components, which we procure directly from domestic and
overseas manufacturers as well as authorized distributors. We maintain long-term
partnerships with key suppliers and collaborate with them from the R&D stage on material
selection and product design. For certain projects, suppliers provide customized material
development, enhancing our product competitiveness and supply chain resilience.
Our Suppliers
Supply Chain Management
We have established a comprehensive supplier management system that covers the full
lifecycle of supplier engagement, including onboarding, daily oversight, performance
evaluation, and elimination mechanisms, to ensure the stability, quality, and compliance of
our supply chain. The details of this supplier management system are set forth as below:

Supplier Onboarding. We have implemented clear criteria and approval procedures for
the selection of new suppliers. Based on our production and operational requirements, our
supply chain management center identifies potential suppliers through various methods such
as the internet, trade exhibitions, and telephone interviews. Our supply chain management
center conducts a preliminary review of the suppliers’ qualifications, while our new R&D
center verifies the compliance of technical documentation. Once the document review is
successfully completed, our supply chain management center collects preliminary quotations
from suppliers and conducts a comprehensive evaluation and confirmation of pricing.
Suppliers are then requested to provide samples. For certain products or materials,
small-batch validation is required following sample approval before large-scale procurement
can proceed.
Ongoing Supplier Management. As part of our routine supplier oversight, we have
developed detailed standards, including supplier tier classification and sample testing
requirements. We also conduct on-site reviews of suppliers’ manufacturing environments to
ensure their processes meet the quality and regulatory requirements of both domestic and
international markets.

Performance Evaluation and Tiering. Suppliers are evaluated quarterly or annually
basedoncategory.Evaluationcriteriaincludeproductquality,deliveryperformance,pricing,
payment terms, and after-sales service. Composite scores determine supplier ratings across
four tiers. High-performing suppliers are prioritized for new projects, while underperforming
suppliers are subject to corrective actions, downgrading, or removal from the approved list.
Exit and Adjustment Mechanisms. Suppliers failing to meet performance standards are
given a defined period for improvement. If corrective actions are unsuccessful, their
qualificationsmaybedowngradedorrevoked.Oursupplychainmanagementcentermayalso
adjust supplier status based on sample testing results or market conditions.
Quality Control. We also implement measures to continuously monitor the final
product quality. See “— Quality Control”for further details.

Our suppliers primarily include providers for raw materials and equipment, production
consumables, and external R&D and partners. The credit period granted by our major
suppliers is generally between 30 to 90 days.

Salient Terms of General Supply Agreements with Suppliers
Salient terms of our general supply agreements with our major suppliers typically
include:
Terms. The terms of our agreements are typically one year, which can be mutually
extended for one year period by written agreement of both parties.
Pricing and Payment. The framework agreements generally do not specify quantity and
price,whichwesetoutinpurchaseorders.Wetypicallymakepaymentwithin30daysafterwe
receive the invoice.
Assignment. Neither party shall assign its rights and obligations to other parties and
entities without the written consent.
Logistics. The suppliers are typically responsible for the delivery of products to our
designated location specified in each purchase order.
Quality Assurance. Suppliers generally grant a warranty period of one to two years. In
the event of a quality issue arising during the warranty period, the supplier is obliged to
provide a response and resolution or attend to our site to resort the issue.
Product return. We have the right to reject, replace or return products which are
non-conforming with product quality standard, product specifications or quantity with the
order placed.
Confidentiality.BoththesuppliersandourCompanyshallbeobligatedtomaintainthe
confidentiality of all business information, technical data, trade secrets, and other
confidential materials obtained or held by either party during the course of business
collaboration.
Termination. We reserve the right to unilaterally terminate the contract if a force
majeure event persists for more than 30 days and renders the supplier unable to deliver the
products.
Supplier Concentration
Overview of Relationship with E Ink Holdings
In 2010, we entered into a joint development agreement with E Ink Corporation, a
subsidiary of E Ink Holdings, which marked the beginning of a long-term strategic
partnership. Building on this foundation, E Ink Holdings commenced formal business
cooperation with us in 2015, further deepening our commercial ties. In 2018, E Ink Holdings
reinforced this relationship by becoming our shareholder through Chuanqi Optoelectronics
with an equity interest of 2.73%, demonstrating its confidence in our business and
commitment to long-term cooperation. These milestones reflect a strong and enduring
partnership characterized by shared technological development and strategic alignment,
which we believe reduces the risk of possible material adverse change in our relationship.
During the Track Record Period, our purchases from E Ink Holdings were RMB379.0
million, RMB478.1 million and RMB783.9 million, respectively, representing 49.5%, 49.2%
and 52.7%, respectively, of our total purchases for the same periods. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, we did not have any minimum supply agreements with E Ink Holdings and
except for the aforementioned joint development agreement, we did not sign any long-term
agreementwithEInkHoldingsoritsgroupcompanies.AccordingtoCIC,sucharrangements
are in line with industry practices as major suppliers such as E Ink Holdings generally adjust
their capacity allocation according to the year’s order size.
As E Ink Holdings was our major supplier of e-ink films during the Track Record
Period, if our relationship with E Ink Holdings is either terminated, interrupted, or modified
in any way adverse to us, there may be material interruptions to our operations and business.
See “Risk Factors — Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry — Our supplier
concentration exposes us to supply chain risks, the loss of which could adversely affect our
business.”

BUSINESS
Reasons for Reliance on E Ink Holdings
DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,weprimarilyprocurede-inkfilmsandprotectivefilms
from E Ink Holdings, a global leader in e-paper display technology. E Ink Holdings is widely
recognizedastheoriginatorandcommercialleaderof electrophoretice-papertechnologyand
the principal global supplier of e-ink film used in e-readers, electronic shelf labels, signage,
and other applications.
During the Track Record Period, in addition to our purchase of e-ink films directly
from E Ink Holdings, we also procured e-ink films from six other suppliers which, to the best
of our knowledge, also procured such raw materials directly or indirectly from E Ink
Holdings. According to CIC, such arrangements with e-ink films procurement are not
uncommon for the e-paper display industry given E Ink Holdings’ market dominance in the
area of e-ink film supplies. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable
Date, we sourced all e-ink films directly or indirectly from E Ink Holdings.
According to CIC, there is one alternative e-ink film supplier in the market which
possesses the necessary technology and production capacity to meet our requirements at
potentially comparable commercial terms and which accounted for substantially all of the
remaining market share apart from E Ink Holdings. The reasons for us to procure e-ink films
exclusively from E Ink Holdings and its distributors during the Track Record Period instead
of also procuring from this alternative supplier are due to the following considerations:
First, according to CIC, the supply of key upstream raw materials for the e-paper
industry (e.g., e-ink film) is highly concentrated. Due to the highly specialized nature of
electrophoretic e-paper technology and the lack of widely available substitutes for e-ink film,
it is common practice in the e-paper industry for manufacturers, including us, to source e-ink
film exclusively from E Ink Holdings (including its distributors), which is recognized as the
originator and global leader in this technology.
Second,EInkHoldingsistheleaderintheglobale-inkfilmindustry,holdingover90%
market share in 2025 in terms of revenue, according to CIC. E Ink Holdings dominates the
global e-ink film industry primarily due to its proprietary electrophoretic display technology
and extensive patent portfolio, which create high entry barriers for competitors. Its products
deliver proven and mature performance in terms of contrast ratio, refresh rate, zero-power
image retention, environmental durability and long-term reliability. These qualities are
long-validated by the market and fully meet our requirements for high performance (such as
keyperformancemetricsof drivestabilityandbatch-to-batchconsistency)andprovidebetter
safeguardsforthequalityandefficiencyof ourmassproductionof modules.EInkHoldings’
first-mover advantage and long-term partnerships with major e-reader brands and retailers
have secured market leadership which makes it almost inevitable for e-paper display module
producers like us to first come to E Ink Holdings (and its distributors) over other suppliers.
Third,giventhetechnicalcomplexity,stringentqualityrequirements,andconcentrated
upstream supply of key raw materials such as e-ink film, procuring from E Ink Holdings
ensures consistent product quality, stable supply, and alignment with industry standards.
Furthermore, to secure manufacturing capacity and maintain centralized management of
critical components, reliance on a limited number of strategic suppliers, particularly E Ink
Holdings, is in line with prevailing industry practice. This is because there are variations in
material formulations, driving waveforms and process parameters among different e-ink film
suppliers. To maintain production process stability and product consistency, module
manufacturers typically prefer to establish deep collaboration with a single primary supplier
and optimize their processes around that supplier’s material system. According to CIC, this
practice is relatively common within the industry and helps reduce costs and risks associated
with switching between multiple material suppliers.

Reliance on E Ink Holdings
Our Directors are of the view, and the Sole Sponsor concurs, that our Group’s reliance
on E Ink Holdings has no material adverse impact on our Group and the likelihood of any
material adverse change or termination of our relationship with E Ink Holdings is minimal.
These are based on the following considerations:
Long-term and Stable Relationship. We have maintained a long-term, stable, and
mutuallybeneficialcollaborationwithEInkHoldingssince2010throughitssubsidiary,EInk
Corporation. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had
notexperiencedanydisputes,conflicts,ormaterialdisagreementswithEInkHoldings,which
would underscore the stability, harmony, and mutual trust in our long-standing relationship.
This consistent record of smooth cooperation reflects both parties’ commitment to
maintaining a reliable and collaborative partnership. Furthermore, we have never failed to
renew agreements with E Ink Holdings. The uninterrupted renewal of these agreements over
multiple years demonstrates the continuity, reliability, and strategic importance of this
partnership to both parties, providing strong assurance that our relationship with E Ink
Holdings is firmly established and unlikely to materially adversely change or terminate.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we sourced all e-ink
films directly or indirectly from E Ink Holdings. According to CIC, such arrangements with
e-ink films procurement are not uncommon for the e-paper display industry given E Ink
Holdings’ market dominance in the area of e-ink film supplies even though there is one
alternative e-ink film supplier available for such raw materials outside of the E Ink Holdings
supply-chain system.
E Ink Holdings’ Vested Interest. E Ink Holdings has been our shareholder since 2018,
which not only reinforces its vested interest in our continued growth and success but also
reflects a strong strategic alignment between both parties. As a shareholder, E Ink Holdings
benefits directly from our business performance, creating a shared incentive to maintain a
stable and long-term partnership. This equity relationship fosters deeper collaboration,
mutual trust, and commitment to joint development initiatives, further solidifying the
foundation of our cooperation and reducing the likelihood of possible material adverse
change or termination of our relationship. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we were not
awareof anyexpressedintentionfromEInkHoldingstoincreaseitsequityinvestmentsinour
Group. We will continue to explore means to strengthen our on-going collaboration with E
InkHoldingsonmultiplefronts,coveringbusinessandindustryperspectiveswithoutlimiting
only to equity investments.
Effort to Diversify Source of Raw Materials. We have endeavored to implement a
diversification strategy to strengthen our supply chain resilience to the extent practicable and
also in line with industry practices. By engaging multiple suppliers across different product
categories and regions, we aim to reduce dependency on any single supplier and mitigate
potential risks arising from supply disruptions. To further enhance supply chain security, we
continuously optimize resource allocation through long-term partnerships with high-quality
suppliers and a dynamic supplier management system featuring a merit-based elimination
mechanism.Oursuppliernetworkspansmultiplecountriesandregions,forminganintegrated
“domestic + overseas” diversified supply system that significantly improves flexibility,
bargaining power, and risk resistance. This structure ensures continuity of production and
operational stability, providing strong assurance that even in the unlikely event of changes
with major suppliers, our operations will remain robust and uninterrupted.

SALES AND MARKETING
Our marketing strategy prioritizes manufacturing excellence, technology enhancement,
solution integration, and sustainability. Leveraging our core strengths in e-paper R&D and
manufacturing, we deeply integrate technology, application scenarios, and sustainability, and
positionourselvesasabroadere-papersolutionsproviderratherthansolelyadisplaymodule
supplier. By focusing on key verticals such as retail, we deliver high-caliber products that
build market credibility. At the same time, the low power consumption and reusability of
e-paper align with corporate ESG goals, adding tangible green value to our offerings. In the
future, we would accelerate technological advancements in flexible, large-size, and color
e-paper, expand product applications in emerging fields such as the IoT, and build a
data-driven, global, end-to-end marketing system to further strengthen technological
cooperation, broaden scenario-based knowledge, and support a sustainable ecosystem.
As of December 31, 2025, our sales and marketing team consisted of 25 members. The
team works closely with departments including R&D, production and procurement to ensure
supplychainresponsivenessandcustomersatisfaction.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,most
of our revenue was generated through direct sales. Our direct sales team is responsible for
customer development, order management, technical support and after-sales services, which
ensures efficient coordination between product delivery and customer response.
In certain overseas markets, including Japan, South Korea and Europe, we collaborate
with local sales partners based in the respective countries or regions of our customers. These
partners primarily included specialized consulting firms, regional trading companies and
established manufacturers in the display and LED technology sectors. Their principal
businesses include providing advisory services for electronic components and display
solutions, facilitating international trade and distribution of display-related products, and
manufacturing LED lighting, display systems and semiconductor components. Leveraging
technicalexpertise,globalsupplychainnetworksandadvancedproductioncapabilities,these
partners support market penetration and ensure high-quality solutions for end customers. In
addition, they provide local market and customer insights, assist in marketing and customer
development, help identify product and order requirements, and support us in follow-up
matters such as contract execution, product delivery, quality feedback and payment
collection.Accordingly,perourcollaborationagreement,theyareresponsibleforassistingin

We select distributors for the sale of our e-paper display modules based on a range of
criteria, including business scale, regional distribution capabilities, warehousing capacity,
creditworthiness and commercial reputation, comprehensive market management, sound
marketing plans, and a certain level of technical support capability. We monitor and evaluate

relationships. We maintain a standard buyer-seller relationship with distributors, and enter
intosalescontractswithourdistributorsinthesamemanneraswithourdirectcustomers.We
may also enter into distribution agreements with certain major distributors. Distributors
purchase products directly from us and are considered our customers. We generally do not
impose minimum purchase requirements or sales targets, and distributors are neither
incentivized nor obligated to purchase quantities exceeding end-customer demand. Likewise,
we do not maintain any policy for managing sub-distributors.
Our distributors purchase e-paper display modules from us and maintain their own
inventories. We exercise strict control over our distribution channels and mitigate the risk of
channel stuffing by partnering with carefully selected distributors. We believe the risk of
channel stuffing within our distribution network is low, given that (i) we maintain a
contractual buyer-seller relationship with distributors; and (ii) we generally do not permit
productreturnsunlessduetoqualityissuesattributabletous.Weassessourdistributorswith
respect to sales performance, initiation of new projects, key customer support, operational
efficiency and compliance status. As we typically maintain long-term relationships with our
distributors, the proportion of non-recurring sales during the Track Record Period was
relatively low.

Pricing
We price our products based on various factors, including the costs of the materials,
productioncosts,ordervolumes,financialgoals,competitionandthesizeof displaymodules.
We closely monitor fluctuations in prices of main materials and related raw materials, and
activelyworktoreduceprocurementandproductioncosts,andreassessproductpricinglevels
when necessary. Our framework sales agreements or supplementary agreements include price
adjustment mechanisms, providing us flexibility to adjust product pricing when
supply-demand dynamics or commercial conditions change. We have and may, from time to
time, face low-price strategies adopted by industry peers. Our Directors are of the view that
suchstrategiesdidnothaveamaterialadverseimpactonourbusinessoperationsorfinancial
performanceduringtheTrackRecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticableDate,primarily
because: (i) our customers generally prioritise product stability, consistency, reliability and
delivery capability over price alone, as evidenced by our customer retention rate reaching
82.9%, 95.7% and 98.2% in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively; (ii) we generally maintained a
considerablyhighergrossprofitmarginduringtheTrackRecordPeriodcomparedtoindustry
peers which adopted low-price strategies, while the selling prices of our products were
generally in line with market prices according to CIC; and (iii) our competitive strengths in
technology, product quality, production scale and customer service have enabled us to
compete on the basis of overall value, as reflected in our prominent position in the global
e-paper display industry. The consistent increase in our revenue and net profit during the
Track Record Period further demonstrated that the low-price strategies adopted by certain
industry peers did not materially impair our revenue growth or profitability. Nonetheless,
continued or intensified price competition could, over time, exert downward pressure on the
selling prices of our products or affect our market share, which could in turn have an adverse
impact on our business, operating results and financial condition. For further details, see
“Risk Factors — Risks relating to Our Business and Industry — We are confronted with
competition from other industry players and the pressure of technological iteration.” For
furtherdetailsonoursellingprices,seealso“FinancialInformation—PrincipalComponents
of Consolidated Statements of Profit or Loss and Historical Results of Operations —
Revenue — Sales Volume and Average Selling Price.”

BUSINESS
After-sales Services and Customer Engagement
We are committed to delivering outstanding after-sales services and consistently
improving our customer service system to ensure customer satisfaction and nurture enduring
partnerships. By implementing standardized procedures for complaints and returns, and
involving multiple departments in the process, we ensure prompt and systematic issue
resolution while transforming customer feedback and return data into actionable
improvements that enhance product and service quality.
We adhere to a customer centric approach and have implemented two key internal
procedures:theCustomerComplaintHandlingPolicy《客戶投訴處理規定》andtheCustomer
Return Handling Policy《客戶退貨處理規定》to standardize and enhance customer service
management.
For customer complaint handling, we establish a structured and tiered response
mechanismbasedonissueseveritytoensuretimelyresolutionandefficientclosure.Customer
feedback is classified into three levels: (a) for customer feedback, we provide a response and
corresponding measures within 24 hours; (b) for general complaints, we provide a response
within 24 hours, deliver an improvement plan within three working days, and issue an 8D
report within five working days; and (c) for major complaints, we provide a response within
four hours, deliver an improvement plan within two working days, and issue an 8D report
within five working days.
For returned materials handling, we established a standardized return and rework
process to ensure prompt response, proper classification, and timely replenishment for
defective products. The return handling and rework process is as follows: (a) our returned
materialsteamregistersthereturnedgoodswiththewarehouseandretrievestheproducts;(b)
defectsarere-inspected,andthetopthreeissuesaresubmittedforengineeringanalysiswithin
two days; (c) items are then classified as repairable or non-repairable, with non-repairable
itemsfollowingthescrappingprocessandrepairableitemsundergoingevaluation,afterwhich
repair procedures and required materials are shared with Planning, Production, and Quality
within two days; (d) planning schedules the rework within one day, and the repair team
completesreworkwithinfifteendaysfollowingallstandardinspectionsteps;and(e)oursales
team arranges replenishment to meet customer demand.
We incorporate multiple departments into our after-sales service system to ensure
prompt and effective handling of customer complaints and returns, from initial reporting to
follow-up resolution. This cross-departmental collaboration enables comprehensive tracking
and systematic improvement of product issues, enhancing both product and service quality.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not experience
anymaterialproductreturnorcustomercomplaint,orproductrecallthatadverselyimpacted
our reputation, business operations or financial condition, nor were we subject to any
material product liability claim.
OUR CUSTOMERS
Our customers primarily comprise leading global and domestic providers of smart
retail and IoT display solutions. These customers focus on areas such as electronic shelf
labels, retail automation, in-store digitalization, digital technology integration, e-paper price
tags and related applications. They generally maintain stringent supplier qualification
standards, requiring high levels of product quality, reliability and compliance. We generally
grant a credit period of between 30 to 90 days to our customers.

Key Terms of Agreements with Customers
The following summarizes the salient terms in our framework agreements with
customers:
Scope of Work. The customer commissions us to design, develop, and manufacture
e-paper modules.
Duration. The terms of our agreements are typically around two years.
Purchase Amount. The purchase amount is specified in each purchase order under the
framework agreement.
Delivery and Performance Management. We manufacture and deliver products to
customers in accordance with the requirements specified in the purchase orders. We are
generally responsible for customs clearance, if any. We engage third-party customs brokerage
companies to handle customs filing clearance for our customers.
Pricing and Payment. During the term of the framework agreement, we shall not
unilaterally increase the price of products, and any change in price shall be confirmed in
writing by both parties. Customers are generally required to make payment within 30 to 90
days after delivery or monthly statement.
Product Liability. The products we provide to customers shall meet the relevant quality
requirements. If any loss is caused to the customer due to the failure of our products to meet
such quality standards, we shall be liable for compensation.
Product Return Arrangements. We typically do not allow our customers to return
products to us except for limited reasons, such as product design defects or quality issues.
ProductWarranty.Themanufacturedproductsmustmeetthespecificationsasmutually
agreed, and the product warranty period typically ranges from one to five years.
Confidentiality.BoththecustomerandourCompanyshallbeobligatedtomaintainthe
confidentiality of all business information, technical data, trade secrets, and other
confidential materials obtained or held by either party during the course of business
collaboration.
Termination. The framework agreements may be terminated by mutual consent of the
parties or under certain circumstances, such as a party’s refusal to comply with the terms of
the agreement or in the event of a party’s bankruptcy.

Period were not inter-conditioned, inter-related or otherwise considered as one transaction,
and were conducted in the ordinary course of business and under normal commercial terms.

THIRD-PARTY PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS
Background
During the Track Record Period, certain of our customers (“Customers”) settled their
payments to us through third-party payors (the “Third-Party Payment Arrangements”). In
2023, 2024 and 2025, the number of Customers was four, six and one, respectively. The
revenue attributable to transactions involving Third-Party Payment Arrangements amounted
to approximately RMB6.1 million and RMB9.9 million in 2023 and 2024, respectively,
accounting for 0.6% and 0.9% of our total revenue, respectively. Such amount decreased
significantly to around RMB2,040 in 2025 which only accounted for less than 0.1% of our
totalrevenuefortheyear.Of theabovethird-partypaymentamountsduringtheTrackRecord
Period, a predominant portion occurred in the Chinese mainland, which amounted to
RMB6.0million,RMB9.9millionandnilin2023,2024and2025,respectively,accountingfor
0.6%,0.9%andnilof ourtotalrevenue,respectively.Arelativelyminimalportionoccurredin
Hong Kong through our subsidiary, DKE Hong Kong, which amounted to approximately
RMB55,000,RMB21,000andRMB2,040in2023,2024and2025,respectively,accountingfor
lessthan0.1%of ourtotalrevenueforeachyear.Tothebestknowledgeof ourDirectors,after
making all reasonable inquiries, the Customers and their respective third-party payors are
independent third parties.
Reasons for Utilizing Third-Party Payment Arrangements
The Third-Party Payment Arrangements arose under the following circumstances: (i)
where a customer was unable to settle the payment for goods, such payment was made by its
affiliatedpartyonitsbehalf;and(ii)forcertainoverseascustomerswhopurchasedindividual
samples, we accepted payment through third-party payment platforms for convenience
purposes. The majority of our third-party payment amounts resulted from the first
circumstance. In particular, one such instance related to an aggregate amount of
approximately RMB15.9 million due from one particular customer (“Relevant Customer”)
which was unable to settle its outstanding balance with us due to its deteriorating financial
and business condition. The payment was being settled by the local law enforcement
authorities together with the Relevant Customer’s parent company and its subsidiaries
pursuanttoasettlementagreement.See“RiskFactors—RisksRelatingtoOurOperations—
We may be subject to various risks relating to third-party payment.”
Legality of the Third-Party Payment Arrangements
To the best knowledge of our Directors after making reasonable enquiries that, during
theTrackRecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticableDate,(i)therelevantpaymentswere
based on bona fide underlying transactions and valid contractual relationships; (ii) we had
not encountered any disputes with, nor received any refund request from, any of the
Customers or third party payors, (iii) we had not been subject to any administrative penalties
by any PRC government authorities with respect to the Third-Party Payment Arrangements,
(iv) the pricing, payment and other salient terms of the agreements we entered into with the
Customers were in line with our other customers not involved in the Third-Party Payment
Arrangementsand(v)nothingcametoourattentionthatwouldcauseourDirectorstodoubt
the genuineness of relevant transactions or the good faith of relevant parties involved.

efficiency. We implement comprehensive controls for material inbound (verification, quality

ensuring accuracy, minimizing obsolescence, and supporting our commitment to quality and
operational efficiency. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our inventory turnover days were
approximately 120 days, 124 days and 122 days, respectively.
Our inventory management system adheres to stringent, standardized procedures
acrossallfacilities,includingourproductionfacilityinVietnam,toensureefficientandsecure
handling of materials from raw components to finished goods.

Transfer Pricing Analysis
The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (“OECD”), an
international organization of international cooperation, has issued transfer pricing
guidelines, for multinational enterprises and tax administrations (the “OECD Transfer
Pricing Guidelines”). In line with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, intra-group
transactions should follow the arm’s length principle to avoid distorted taxable income in
different jurisdictions.
For the intra-group transactions between DKE Hong Kong and DKE Fushen, DKE
Longning and DKE Fuyong, our transfer pricing consultant has adopted the transactional
net margin method (“TNMM”) as the transfer pricing method for reviewing the Covered
Transactions,selectingDKEHongKongasthetestedparty.TNMMiscommonlyadoptedto
review intra-group transactions involving tangible goods buy-sell and therefore would be the
mostappropriatetransferpricingmethodtoassesswhetherthetransferpricingarrangements
related to the Covered Transactions were consistent with the arm’s length principle.
Accordingtotheanalysisresultof TNMMmethod,theweightedaverageprofitlevelof
DKE Hong Kong for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months
ended June 30, 2025, fall within the inter-quartile range for the comparable companies.
Based on the above analysis, the transfer pricing consultant has stated that the transfer
pricing arrangement related to the Covered Transactions for the period under review was
consistent with the arm’s length principle.
On this basis, our Directors are of the view that the above-mentioned transfer pricing
arrangements of our Group align with the arm’s length principle according to the OECD
Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
The Company has also established internal policies and procedures for transfer pricing
management, and it has continued to apply such policies and procedures consistently in all
material respects for transfer pricing management after June 30, 2025.
Pursuant to the enterprise special credit reports of DKE Fushen, DKE Longning and
DKE Fuyong, each of DKE Fushen, DKE Longning and DKE Fuyong did not have any
record of illegality or irregularity related to its taxes during the Track Record Period.
Furthermore, pursuant to the certificates issued by the competent tax authorities of DKE
Fushen, DKE Longning and DKE Fuyong, there were no taxes in default for each of DKE
Fushen, DKE Longning and DKE Fuyong as of the Latest Practicable Date.
Our management had been and will continue to closely monitor our Group’s transfer
pricing arrangements including reviewing the reasonableness of the pricing policy of our
transfer pricing arrangements from time to time. However, we cannot assure that our transfer
pricing arrangements will not be subject to review and possible challenge by any relevant tax
authorities in future, even though we believe we have reasonable grounds to defend ourselves
againstsuchpossiblechallenge.See“RiskFactors—RisksRelatingtoFinancial,Accounting
and Tax Matters — We are subject to regulatory risks with respect to our tax compliance”for
further details.

ESG Governance Framework
We have established an ESG governance framework structured across three levels:
decision-making, organizational and operational. The Board of Directors, as the highest
governance body, is responsible for ESG decision-making, and approving our ESG and
climate-related management policies, strategies, objectives, and annual work programs. The
Board also assesses, prioritizes, and manages material ESG risks and opportunities, and
ensures appropriate oversight of significant ESG and climate-related issues. The Board
convenesmeetingsatleastbiannuallytodiscussESG-relatedmatters,overseeingandannually
reviewing ESG performance and progress towards ESG targets.
The organizational level is headed by the Board Secretary as a leader of the ESG
Working Group, with members comprising the director of the Quality Management Centre,
the deputy general manager of the Human Resources and Administration Management
Centre, and the deputy general manager of the Manufacturing Centre. The organizational
level is responsible for (i) formulating ESG and climate-related management policies,
strategies, annual work plans and targets for Board approval; (ii) identifying, assessing and
managing material ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities; and (iii) continuously
monitoringandreviewingESGandclimate-relatedperformanceandtargetprogresstoensure
allESGmattersareproperlymanagedandimplemented.TheESGWorkingGroupreportsto
the Board on our ESG matters at least semi-annually. The operational level comprises
functional departments responsible for (i) compiling internal policies, systems, and
performance indicators related to ESG; and (ii) advancing and executing all ESG and
climate-relatedinitiatives.TheoperationallevelreportsregularlytotheESGWorkingGroup.
Directors have received training on ESG matters, and we have engaged external ESG
advisers to provide the requisite ESG expertise.
Materiality Assessment
To understand the expectations and needs of our stakeholders and to accurately assess
the materiality of various ESG issues for our operations, we engaged an independent
third-party ESG consultant. This engagement referenced Appendix C2 of the Main Board
Listing Rules of the Stock Exchange, the ESG Reporting Code, and industry-specific
concerns. The consultant conducted a materiality assessment by collecting stakeholder
feedback through questionnaire surveys. We prioritized material issues based on our analysis
of their importance to both stakeholders and the company. The materiality assessment
processinvolvesidentifyingpotentialESGissuesrelevanttoouroperationsandstakeholders,
engaging a wide range of stakeholders through questionnaires to evaluate the significance of
each issue, analyzing their feedback to prioritize key concerns, and reviewing and identifying
material issues for further action and disclosure.
Based on the materiality assessment results, the highly material ESG issues are product
quality and safety, employee rights, occupational health and safety, customer service, and
remuneration and benefits. For details on how we address and manage these issues, see “—
Quality Control”, “— Environmental, Social and Governance — Social Responsibility” and
“— Sales and Marketing — After-sales Services and Customer Engagement.”

We place great emphasis on the environmental impact of our operations and actively
implement our environmental policies. At the same time, to support China’s “dual-carbon
goals” of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, we focus on “strengthening environmental
protection, focusing on pollution prevention, conserving energy, reducing consumption and
emissions,andpromotingcleanproduction.”Inourdailyoperations,weproactivelyadoptthe
following environmental measures to safeguard the environment and achieve sustainable
environmental development.
Environmental Management
We strictly adhere to the Environmental Protection Law of the People’s Republic of
China and other relevant environmental protection laws and regulations. All subsidiaries
withinourGrouphaveobtainedISO14001EnvironmentalManagementSystemcertification.
WehaveestablishedtheEnvironmental/OccupationalHealthandSafetyManagementManual
and Environmental Health and Safety Policy, rigorously controlling resource utilization,
wastedischarge,energyconsumptionandotheraspectsthroughoutproductionoperations.To
prevent and address potential environmental issues, we conduct regular environmental risk
assessments and employee environmental training. These focus on key areas such as
hazardous chemicals, energy conservation and emissions reduction, and waste disposal,
thereby continuously enhancing our environmental management standards. During the Track
RecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticableDate,wehadnotbeen,inanymaterialrespect,
in violation of any applicable environmental laws and regulations in China, according to our
PRC Legal Advisors, and in Vietnam, according to our Vietnam Legal Advisors, respectively.
We have adopted the 5.0 digital intelligent factory concept. We also implemented
integrated management systems such as enterprise resource planning (ERP) across our
production lines and relevant business units. This digital transformation enhances our
capabilitiesingreenenergyconservationandautomatedprocesssynergy,enablingthephasing
out of high-energy-consumption, obsolete equipment to achieve green, low-carbon
production.BoththeJiaxingComprehensiveBondedZonebaseandtheJiaxingheadquarters
base have been certified as “Green Factories”by Jiaxing Municipal Bureau of Economy and
Information Technology.
Energy Conservation and Consumption Reduction
WehaveformulatedandimplementedpoliciessuchastheEnergyandResourceControl
Procedure and the Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction Control Procedure. The
Human Resources and Administration Management Centre is responsible for developing
energy-savingandconsumption-reductionplans,organizingrelevantdepartmentstoestablish
management teams dedicated to energy conservation. We have established specific electricity
consumption targets and installed smart meters. Dedicated personnel are assigned to oversee
electricityusagefromthedistributionroomsatallconsumptionpointstoensureadherenceto
our energy-saving protocols. Furthermore, we have replaced fluorescent lighting across our
officesandproductionworkshopswithenergy-efficientLEDfixtures.Wealsotrainpersonnel
operating energy-consuming equipment to learn energy-saving operational methods, set
distinct air conditioning temperatures for winter and summer, and assign dedicated staff to
schedule lighting in communal areas. Furthermore, in accordance with our Sustainable
Procurement Policy, we prioritize suppliers and products meeting environmental standards.
We aligned our actions with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and
theMinistryof Finance’sNoticeonIssuingthe2023-2024ActionPlanforStabilizingGrowth
in the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry, and are committed to achieving
environmental protection and energy conservation through technological innovation. By
employing green design principles, our e-paper displays consume power only during content
refreshes, thereby minimizing electricity usage during operation. Furthermore, we encourage
users of e-paper products to obtain new functionalities via software updates rather than
replacing hardware, extending product lifespans and consequently reducing resource
consumption.

BUSINESS
Water Resources Management
We establish annual water consumption targets and allocate them to individual
departments. Dedicated personnel inspect and maintain water pipelines to minimize water
wastage.Throttlevalveshavebeeninstalledinkeywater-consumingareassuchasthecanteen.
Staff are required to ensure taps are fully turned off after use. The Equipment Management
Department is responsible for conducting inspections to ensure that all valves and water
supply pipes remain leak-free.
Waste Management
We have established the Hazardous Waste Management System and Solid Waste
Management System, implementing a waste classification framework to ensure meticulous
management of all waste streams. Solid waste is categorized into non-recyclable and
recyclable materials, with professional agencies contracted for recovery and processing.
Specific requirements are stipulated for transportation, utilization, and treatment phases to
ensure proper disposal. Additionally, we maintain declarations and registrations for solid
waste generation volumes and hazardous waste sources.
The primary hazardous waste materials generated from our production operations
include spent activated carbon, contaminated cloths, and specialized packaging materials.
Our Hazardous Waste Management System clarifies the identification, collection, storage,
and disposal of such waste. We maintain a dedicated hazardous waste inventory, which
recordstheintakedate,type,andquantityof allhazardouswaste.Allwasteiscategorisedand
stored in a dedicated, purpose built temporary storage facility. This facility is designed to be
impermeable, sheltered from wind, rain, and sunlight, and is under dedicated personnel
management.Weengagethird-partycontractorswithvalidbusinesslicencesandtherequisite
hazardous waste processing permits to recycle and dispose of this waste. For the
transportation of hazardous waste, we operate a mandatory manifest system in accordance
with the Measures for the Management of the Hazardous Waste Transfer Manifest to ensure
the proper transfer and final disposal of all hazardous waste.
Emissions and Wastewater Management
We have formulated and implemented the Waste Emissions Management System,
assigning dedicated personnel to conduct daily inspections of the company’s emissions and
wastewater discharge points. Annual testing is commissioned to qualified third-party
institutions.
Regarding emissions, we adhere to standards such as the Comprehensive Emission
Standard for Air Pollutants (GB 16297-1996) for managing emissions. Emissions are treated
using methods including activated carbon adsorption and baghouse dust collection before
beingreleasedincompliancewithregulatoryrequirements.Asforwastewater,wegenerateno
production wastewater. Domestic sewage undergoes on-site pre-treatment before being
discharged into the municipal sewage network in compliance with standards.
Metrics
Our greenhouse gas emissions scope encompasses Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3. Scope
1 refers to direct emissions, mainly from the combustion of fossil fuels at stationary and
mobile sources; Scope 2 refers to indirect emissions, primarily from the consumption of
externally procured electricity. Scope 3 emissions represent indirect greenhouse gas emissions
from sources not owned or controlled by us. Our primary Scope 3 emission sources include
greenhouse gas emissions from the electricity consumed in processing potable water and
wastewater,emissionsfromwastepaperdisposedof inlandfills,andemissionsgeneratedfrom
employee business travel by air.
