Environmental Targets
Wearecommittedtoachievingourenergy-savingandenvironmentalprotectiontargets.
Using 2025 as the baseline, we aim to achieve by 2030 a 5% reduction in electricity and water
consumption per RMB10,000 of revenue, a 5% reduction in both non-hazardous solid waste
and hazardous waste generation per RMB10,000 of revenue, and a 5% reduction in
greenhouse gas emissions per RMB10,000 of revenue.
To achieve these targets, we have integrated measures promoting low-carbon practices,
resource conservation and environmental protection into our business activities. See “—
Environmental, Social and Government — Environment”for relevant disclosures.
Climate Change
We recognize that climate change poses risks to our business operations. Consequently,
we have systematically identified and assessed these risks, implemented targeted mitigation
measures, and incorporated these into our Risk Assessment and Opportunity Response
Matrix.Thisframeworkestablishesclearperformanceindicatorsanddelineatesdepartmental
responsibilities to ensure that climate-related risks are effectively managed.
As the production of e-paper display modules relies on a stable power supply, we have
identified floods and cyclones as acute physical risks. These events may cause power outages
or damage to surrounding buildings, directly impacting normal operations. Severe weather
may also disrupt employee commutes and supply chain operations, leading to business
interruptions. To address these risks, we have established and implemented the Emergency
Preparedness and Response Control Procedure and the Contingency Plan Measures,
conductingdrillsatleastannually.Suppliersareassessedandauditedthroughsystemssuchas
theSupplierSelectionandEvaluationProcedure,ensuringmostmaterialshaveatleasttwoor
more suppliers. Emergency power equipment is deployed within the factory. Specific safety
measures are established for different levels of severe weather.
Extreme temperatures, as a chronic physical risk, may lead to increased energy
consumptionincoolingsystems,reducedoperationalefficiency,andheightenedprobabilityof
damaging fixed equipment and causing property loss. High-temperature environments may
also jeopardize the health and productivity of outdoor workers, and exacerbate the risk of
equipmentfailureandpropertydamage.Ourprimarycountermeasuresincludeimplementing
contingency plans and conducting annual drills; adopting energy-efficient cooling systems;
enhancing the energy efficiency of temperature control equipment; and establishing
emergency protocols for extreme heat events.
Regarding transition risks, as regulatory authorities impose increasingly stringent
requirements for climate-related disclosures, sustainability disclosure obligations and
compliance costs may rise. Failure to meet expectations could adversely affect brand image
andreputation,therebynegativelyimpactingoperatingrevenue.Toaddresspolicy,regulatory
and reputational risks, we have implemented the Legal, Regulatory and Other Requirements
Compliance Evaluation Control Procedure to ensure operations remain compliant with local
laws and regulations, and enhancing climate information transparency through regular
disclosure of greenhouse gas reduction progress to stakeholders.
Rapid advances in low-carbon and energy-saving technologies risk reducing
competitiveness if we lag in upgrades. To mitigate this, we have implemented the Greenhouse
Gas Control Procedure and the Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction Control
Procedure,whilecloselymonitoringregulatorydevelopmentstostrengthenclimatedisclosure
and ensure compliance. To address market risks arising from increasing customer focus on
climate issues, we have also established a sustainability strategy and a three-year
environmental compliance plan to enhance green, low-carbon management and better meet
market expectations.

LEGAL PROCEEDINGS AND COMPLIANCE
Legal Proceedings
From time to time, we may be subject to legal proceedings, investigations and claims
incidental to the conduct of our business. As of the Latest Practicable Date, there was one
legal proceeding involving one of our subsidiaries with a claim amount exceeding RMB10
million which remained unsettled and we were the defendants. We set out below summary of
the case:
On May 30, 2024, Jiaxing Rongda Construction Co., Ltd. filed a construction contract
claim against our subsidiary, Fuyong Technology, in the Jiashan County People’s Court for
unpaid construction fees and liquidated damages and sought to hold our Company and
Fuyong Technology jointly and severally liable. The dispute is over the amount of additional
project costs (hence additional construction fees) arising from design changes under the
construction contract. We did not deliberately delay the payment of the construction fees
without cause and our Directors did not play any role in deliberately delaying such payment
either. On November 3, 2025, the claimant amended its claim to approximately RMB41.5
million, comprising RMB20.0 million of certified outstanding balance and RMB21.5 million
of additional costs arising from design changes identified by the court-appointed appraisal
institution. On June 16, 2026, the court rendered a final judgment ordering us to pay the
claimant the outstanding payment for the construction fees of RMB37.7 million (tax
inclusive) plus overdue interest within a prescribed period from the judgement effective date.
The total amount payable by us pursuant to the judgement is RMB36.4 million (excluding
tax),including(a)RMB34.6millionof outstandingamountfortheconstructionfees,and(b)
RMB1.8 million of overdue interests. Out of the RMB36.4 million, RMB25.7 million has
been recorded as other payables on our consolidated statement of financial position as of
December 31, 2025 and the difference of RMB10.7 million is recorded as provisions on our
consolidated statement of financial position as of December 31, 2025. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, we were yet to settle the outstanding amount and will do so within the
prescribed period in accordance with the final judgment.

Risk Management
Effective risk management is crucial to our sustainable development. We have
established comprehensive, multi-dimensional risk control systems that integrate internal
controls into daily operations. Our Board is collectively responsible for establishing and
implementing these risk management mechanisms and for overseeing our overall risk
management framework. The control system is composed as follows:
Financial Reporting Risk Management
To effectively manage financial reporting risks, we have implemented comprehensive
accounting policies covering financial management and financial statement preparation.
Thesepoliciesaresupportedbyestablishedprocedures,andourfinancedepartmentregularly
reviews management accounts in accordance with them. We have established an Audit
Committee to oversee and review our financial reporting processes and internal control
system.Inaddition,wealsoestablishedanAuditandComplianceCenter,itisresponsiblefor
designing the internal control evaluation report, assessing internal supervision.
Compliance Risk Management
We have established effective compliance risk management procedures to identify and
manage compliance risks and ensure adherence to applicable laws and regulations. Our
management team actively engages in governance and risk discussions, oversees the internal
control system, and is primarily responsible for implementing major event reporting and
decision-making processes. Under these procedures, our legal team drafts and reviews key
contracts, participates in negotiations, handles litigation and arbitration, provides legal
advice,andcentrallymanagesnon-HRandnon-financialcontracts.Ourlegalteamalsoleads
theresolutionof legaldisputesandplaysakeyroleinprotectingourtrademarks,patents,and
other intellectual property.
Information Security Risk Management
We place significant emphasis on information compliance and security, and have
established a comprehensive information management system. Our employees access
information systems through their designated accounts with role-based permissions, enabling
tiered control over sensitive data, including ownership information, management data, and
other confidential information. Strict access controls and complete audit trails ensure the
integrity and security of system operations. Our Information Technology Department is fully
responsible for the planning, development, daily operation, maintenance, security
management, network operations, and hardware infrastructure support of our information
systems. IT roles have been clearly defined and segmented according to functional
responsibilities, ensuring stable, secure, and efficient system performance.
Our business departments and subsidiaries operate in an integrated and coordinated
mannerwithinastrategicframeworkandcentralizedcontrolsystem.Weadoptamanagement
model that combines centralized oversight with moderate delegation of authority: the
headquarters retains centralized control over strategic decision-making, major investments
and financing, key personnel appointments, the establishment of uniform policies, and the
approval of high-risk matters, while subsidiaries are granted operational flexibility within
approved budgets for day-to-day operations and regional procurement, ensuring clear
accountability and efficient execution. At the same time, we have established mandatory
reportingmechanismstoensurethatsubsidiariespromptlyandaccuratelyescalatesignificant
risks or opportunities, thereby supporting proactive group-wide decision-making and
effective risk management. This balanced approach effectively aligns operational agility with
corporate control, underpinning our sustainable and high-quality growth.

Information voluntarily provided by suppliers or customers: including basic information

Data generated during business operations: including ERP system transaction records,

External Operational Data

Consent
Thecollectionof theaboveinformationisconductedwithpriorconsentof therelevant
parties and within the reasonable scope of business needs, and in strict compliance with
applicable laws and regulations. We undertake to manage and use customer and supplier data
in accordance with applicable laws, and to adopt reasonable measures to prevent
unauthorized use, loss or leakage of such data. Except as required by law or under
circumstances prescribed by applicable regulations, we will not disclose any sensitive data to
third parties without prior approval from customers or suppliers.
According to Vietnam Legal Advisors, with respect to employee data in DKE Vietnam,
employees are required to provide their information when entering into labor contracts;
therefore, DKE Vietnam is exempted from obtaining separate consents from employees.
Similarly, for the collection of business data for operational purposes, it is common practice
in Vietnam for companies to proactively provide such data for the purposes of introducing
themselves and procuring contracts; therefore, DKE Vietnam is also not required to obtain
additional consents in these circumstances.

secure data removal. We also utilize hyper-converged backup appliances for robust data
backupanddisasterrecovery.Ourinformationsecuritymanagementframeworkincorporates
policies on system operation, password management, trade secret protection, and document
control, collectively ensuring compliance with high information security standards.

TRADE RESTRICTIONS AND TARIFF
U.S. Export Control Implications
The U.S. export control framework is established under federal law, primarily through
the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”), which are administered by the Bureau of
Industry and Security (“BIS”) within the Department of Commerce. The EAR regulates the
export, reexport, and transfer of commercial, dual-use, and certain military items, including
hardware, software, and technology. Its jurisdiction covers (i) U.S.-origin items; (ii) items in
the U.S. or move in transit through the U.S.; (iii) certain foreign-made items containing more
than de minimis controlled U.S. content; and (iv) foreign-produced items that are the direct
product of specified U.S. technology or software.
Depending on the nature of the item, destination country, end-use, and end-user, prior
authorization from BIS may be required for transactions involving items subject to the EAR.
BISmaintainsseveralrestricted-partylists,includingtheEntityList,whichdesignatesforeign
entities such as companies, research institutions, government and private organizations, and
individuals for enhanced trade restrictions. Listed parties are generally restricted from
accessing U.S.-origin goods, software, and technology, as well as items containing controlled
U.S.-origin content and certain foreign-made products derived from designated U.S.
technology or equipment.

The International Sanctions Implications
The U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”)
administers and enforces economic sanctions against designated foreign countries, entities,
and individuals. These sanctions are established to advance U.S. foreign policy and national
security objectives, with significant variations across different sanctions programs. Such
programsgenerallyapplyto“U.S.persons”asdefinedintherelevantregulations,aswellasto
transactions with a U.S. nexus.
TheUnitedNationsSecurityCouncil(“UNSC”)imposesmandatorysanctionsregimes,
whicharebindingonallUNmemberstatesandprimarilytargetthreatstointernationalpeace
andsecurity.TheEUenactssanctionsvialegallybindingCouncilDecisionsandRegulations,
which are directly applicable across all member states. The UK administers its sanctions
through the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (“OFSI”) and consolidated lists
under its post-Brexit statutory framework. Australia implements sanctions through the
Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, giving effect to both UN obligations and
autonomous measures via its domestic legislation. Such regimes typically function by
designating specific targets and prohibiting dealings with them, with enforcement carried out
by national authorities.

U.S. Outbound Investment Rules Implications
TheU.S.outboundinvestmentreviewmechanisminforceisnarrowlytargetedatcertain
types of investments in the country and typically the restrictions target sensitive technologies
and products critical for military, intelligence, mass-surveillance, or cyber-enabled
capabilities. If no covered activity is involved in the transaction, then the transaction is not
within the jurisdictional scope of the U.S. outbound investment review.
As we are principally engaged in the research and development, production and sale of
e-paper display modules, our business does not fall within any definition of covered activity,
including semiconductor and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, or
artificial intelligence. Thus, as advised by our International Compliance Legal Counsel, our
business scope has not fallen within the definition of the Covered Activities and we are not a
Covered Foreign Person as defined under the Final Rule and the frequently asked questions
published by the U.S. Department of the Treasury on December 23, 2025.
The Tariff Implications
Regarding the direct impact of the U.S. tariff policies, based on our historical export
data, sales to the United States have represented an immaterial portion of our revenue, which
amounted to approximately RMB30,000, RMB160,000, and RMB19,000 in 2023, 2024 and
2025,respectively,representinglessthan0.01%of ourtotalrevenueforeachyearof theTrack
Record Period. Tariffs imposed on products exported to the United States are contractually
bornebythepurchasersof ourproducts,andaccordingly,wedonotprimarilybearsuchtariff
costs.Forourprocurementof rawmaterialsoriginatingfromtheU.S.,a10%retaliatorytariff
on goods originating from the U.S. will be applicable. Specifically, the raw materials we
procured originating from the U.S. in 2023, 2024, and 2025 amounted to approximately
RMB12.3 million, RMB41.3 million and RMB70.4 million, respectively, representing
approximately 1.6%, 4.3% and 4.7% of our total procurement for the corresponding years.
Therefore, our Directors are of the view, and the Sole Sponsor concurs, that U.S. tariffs and
Chinese retaliatory tariffs have not had any direct material adverse impact on our business
operations.
Regarding the indirect impact of the U.S. tariff policies, based on our historical export
data, we are not able to ascertain the specific extent to which our downstream customers
incorporate our products into their end-products for export to the U.S. However, since the
implementationof U.S.tariff measuresagainstChinainApril2025,ouroverallsaleshavenot
experienced any significant changes or material fluctuations. Therefore, our Directors are of
theviewthattheU.S.tariffshavenothadanyindirectmaterialadverseimpactonourbusiness
operations. For our procurement of products that incorporate U.S.-origin components, the
procurementcostof theseproductshasremainedstableandhasnotexperiencedanymaterial
increase despite the relevant tariff policies. Therefore, our Directors are of the view, and the
Sole Sponsor concurs, that Chinese retaliatory tariffs have not had any indirect material
adverse impact on our business operations.

IMPACT OF COVID-19
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not
experience any material disruption to our ordinary business operations as a result of the
COVID-19 pandemic. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our total revenue amounted to RMB1,024.2
million, RMB1,151.6 million and RMB1,713.0 million, respectively, and our sales volume
recorded sustained growth during the Track Record Period reaching 56.1 million units, 67.1
millionunitsand124.5millionunits,respectively.Inaddition,wecontinuedtostrengthenour
production capacity throughout the Track Record Period. For further details, see “—
Production — Production Bases.” Moreover, our core operational areas, including R&D,
product iteration, product delivery and customer engagement, remained on schedule without
any significant delays. In view of the foregoing, our Directors are of the view that the
COVID-19 pandemic did not have any material adverse impact on our business operations or
financial performance during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date.

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE CODE
Our Company is committed to achieving a high standard of corporate governance with
a view to safeguarding the interests of our Shareholders. To accomplish this, our Company
intendstocomplywiththeCorporateGovernanceCodesetoutinAppendixC1totheListing
RulesandtheModelCodeforSecuritiesTransactionsbyDirectorsof ListedIssuerssetoutin
Appendix C3 to the Listing Rules after the Listing.
Pursuant to code provision C.2.1 of Part 2 of the Corporate Governance Code,
companies listed on the Stock Exchange are expected to comply with, but may choose to
deviate from the requirement that the responsibilities between the chairman and the general
managershouldbesegregatedandshouldnotbeperformedbythesameindividual.Wedonot
haveaseparateChairmanandgeneralmanager,andMr.ZhouAijuncurrentlyperformsthese
two roles. The Board believes that vesting the roles of both the Chairman and general
manager in the same person has the benefit of ensuring consistent leadership within our
Group and enables more effective and efficient overall strategic planning for our Group,
taking into consideration that our Group is currently experiencing a period of rapid growth
and requires strategic continuity and stability for the implementation of key initiatives,
including the construction of the manufacturing facility in Vietnam, the research and
development of full-color and flexible e-paper display technologies, as well as market
expansion.Thecombinedrolesstreamlinereportinglinesandreduceinternalcommunication
layers, thereby enhancing the speed and effectiveness of decision-making and responses to
marketopportunities,technologicalchallengesandoperationalmatters.OurBoardconsiders
that the balance of power and authority for the present arrangement will not be impaired in
this regard. Our Company also considers that the leadership of Mr. Zhou, as a Controlling
Shareholderandtechnicalleader,bringsirreplaceableindustryexperience,technicalforesight
and a comprehensive understanding of our Company’s business, allowing his strategic vision
to be translated directly into execution and maximizing leadership effectiveness. Our Board
will continue to review and consider splitting the roles of the Chairman and the general
managerof ourCompanyif andwhenitisappropriatetakingintoaccountthecircumstances
of our Group as a whole.

BOARD DIVERSITY POLICY
We have adopted the board diversity policy which sets out the objective and approach
forachievingandmaintainingthediversityof ourBoardinordertoenhanceitseffectiveness.
In accordance with the board diversity policy, our Company seeks to achieve board diversity
by taking into account a number of factors, including but not limited to gender, age, cultural
and educational background, professional experience, skills, knowledge and/or length of
service. The ultimate selection of Board candidates will be based on merit and potential
contributiontoourBoardhavingdueregardtothebenefitsof diversityonourBoardandalso
the specific needs of our Company without focusing on a single diversity aspect. Our
Directors have a balanced mix of knowledge and skills, including overall management and
strategic development as well as knowledge and experience in areas such as investment and
businessmanagement.Theyobtaineddegreesinvariousareasincludingengineering,business
administrationandlaws.Furthermore,ourBoardhasadiverseageandgenderrepresentation.
OurBoardcurrentlycomprisesonefemaleDirectorandeightmaleDirectors,rangingfrom31
years old to 60 years old.
With regards to gender diversity on our Board, we recognize the particular importance
of gender diversity. We have taken and will continue to take steps to promote and enhance
gender diversity at all levels of our Company, including but without limitation at our Board
and senior management levels. We will maintain a focus on gender diversity when recruiting
staff atthemidtoseniorlevelsoastodevelopapipelineof potentialfemalesuccessorstoour
Board.OurGroupwillalsoidentifyandselectseveralfemaleindividualswithadiverserange
of skills,experienceandknowledgeindifferentfieldsfromtimetotime,andmaintainalistof
such female individuals who possess qualities to become our Board members, which will be
reviewed by our nomination committee periodically to maintain gender diversity of our
Board. Taking into account our existing business model and specific needs as well as the
different background of our Directors, the composition of our Board satisfies our board
diversity policy.
Upon the Listing, the Nomination Committee will from time to time discuss and agree
on expected goals to ensure board diversity, and review and, where necessary, update the
board diversity policy to ensure that the policy remains effective. Our Company will disclose
the biographical details of each Director and report on the implementation of the board
diversity policy (including whether we have achieved board diversity) in its annual corporate
governance report.

HIGHEST-PAID INDIVIDUALS
Our Directors and senior management members who receive remuneration from our

Our Directors recognize the importance of good corporate governance in protection of

measures have been put in place to manage conflicts of interest between our Group and our
Controlling Shareholders and to protect minority Shareholders’interests after the Listing.

In accordance with the PRC Company Law, the shares issued prior to any public
offering of shares by a company cannot be transferred within 12 months from the date on
which such publicly offered shares are listed and traded on the relevant stock exchange. As
such, the Shares issued by our Company prior to the issue of H Shares will be subject to such
statutory restriction on transfer within a period of one year from the Listing Date.

largestglobale-paperdisplaymanufacturerbyrevenuein2025,withamarketshareof 20.8%,
and the largest global commercial e-paper display manufacturer by revenue, with a market

underscoring our market position in the industry.
Over the past 15 years, we have accumulated experience in the e-paper display industry
andbuiltcapabilitiesinproprietarydesignandmanufacturingof e-paperdisplaymodules.We

afullspectrumof displaycolorsandsizes.Ourproductportfolioisusedindiverseapplication
scenarios including smart retail, smart offices, smart education, smart logistics, smart
transportation, e-readers and emerging applications.

KEY FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our results of operations and financial position are affected by a number of factors,
including those factors set out in the section headed “Risk Factors” in this prospectus and
those discussed below:
General Factors
Our results of operations have been, and are expected to continue to be, materially
affected by a number of factors, many of which are beyond our control, including : (a)
development of macroeconomic conditions; (b) government policies and regulations in
relation to the e-paper display industry; (c) international trade policies, geopolitics and trade
protection measures, export control and economic or trade sanctions; (d) evolving
consumptionpatternsandhabitsinChinaandglobally;and(e)weather,naturaldisastersand
climate change.
Specific Factors
The Development of the Industry Where We Operate
Our business focuses on the design, research, development, manufacturing and sale of
e-paper display modules. According to CIC, driven by the continuous expansion of
application scenarios and the rising demand for low-power, green display technologies, the
global e-paper related products increased from RMB32.3 billion in 2021 to RMB74.0 billion
in 2025, with a CAGR of 23.1% during the period. As breakthroughs in low-power display
technology continue and the commercialization of smart application scenarios accelerates,
this market will further unleash its growth potential and application value, with the market
size expected to reach RMB111.7 billion by 2030, maintaining a CAGR of 8.6% during this
period.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our revenue amounted to RMB1,024.2 million, RMB1,151.6
million and RMB1,713.0 million, respectively. We expect the ongoing development of the
e-paper display industry worldwide will continue to spur our future growth. As a prominent
supplier of e-paper display products, we are well positioned to take advantage of the thriving
global e-paper display market.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Relationship with Our Major Customers
Wehaveestablishedandmaintainedlong-termrelationshipswithourmajorcustomers.
Our historical growth was mainly driven by our ability to deepen our relationships with
existing customers and grow our customer base. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue generated
from our five largest customers in each year during the Track Record Period was in aggregate
RMB908.4 million, RMB950.9 million and RMB1,555.0 million, respectively, representing
88.7%, 82.6% and 90.8% of our total revenue, respectively. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue
generated from our largest customer in each year during the Track Record Period was
RMB519.6 million, RMB417.7 million and RMB605.6 million, respectively, representing
50.7%, 36.3% and 35.4% of our total revenue, respectively. Future growth in our business will
depend on our ability to maintain and deepen relationships with our customers. Changes in
relationship with our customers may affect our results of operation and financial condition.
We are committed to expanding our cooperation with our customers. We are among a
limited number of e-paper display manufacturers that have the capability to provide product
matrix with a full range of sizes and colors which can be widely used by our customers in
smart retail, smart office, smart education, smart logistics, smart transportation, e-readers
andemergingapplications.Wecontinuouslypre-emptcustomerneedsbyinnovatingincolors,
product features and application scenarios. We expect to continue to innovate and develop
e-paper display products that address and adapt to our customers’ needs, while also taking
into consideration their budgets. Our ability to continue to perform the foregoing will affect
ourrelationshipwithourcustomers,andinturnaffectourresultsof operationsandfinancial
performance.
Our Ability to Control Costs
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, we incurred cost of sales of RMB862.4 million, RMB969.1
million and RMB1,432.8 million, representing 84.2%, 84.2% and 83.6% of our total revenue,
respectively. Our ability to effectively control our cost of sales while achieving expected
business growth is critical to our profitability. Our primary raw materials include e-ink films,
TFT substrates, driver ICs, protective films, FPCs and other related components. As a result,
the fluctuation in the price of raw materials and consumables has a material impact on our
cost of sales, which in turn will affect our overall gross profit. The majority of our e-paper
displaymodulesshareidenticalcorecomponents,whichenablesustoreducethepriceperunit
through bulk purchase of raw materials. We have established a standardized and efficient
procurementmanagementsystem,andalsohavebuiltlong-term,stablepartnershipswithour
key raw material suppliers.
Our Continual Investment in R&D and Talent
The growth of our revenue depends on our ability to make technological advancements
and develop products that meet the evolving needs of our customers. For the years ended
December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we recorded R&D expenses of RMB39.9 million,
RMB56.0 million and RMB59.0 million, representing 3.9%, 4.9% and 3.4% of our total
revenue, respectively. We view R&D as a core driver of our long-term competitiveness,
scalabilityandproductinnovation.OurR&Dstrategyisbuiltonacommitmenttocontinuous
investment, systematic capability-building and forward-looking technological exploration.
We have established a comprehensive R&D system that integrates experienced inhouse R&D
team, disciplined processes and close collaboration with partners to support the development
of the key technologies in the industry. We have made, and will continue to make, significant
investments in people, technology and R&D, to reinforce our competitive edges and enhance
gross profit margin, thereby solidifying our market position and providing great customer
experience.

Our Ability to Improve Operational Efficiency
Our ability to achieve profitability and to support sustainable growth is dependent on
our ability to further improve our operational efficiency and control total operating expenses
as a percentage of our revenues. For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we
recorded general and administrative expenses of RMB68.1 million, RMB62.3 million and
RMB87.9 million, representing 6.7%, 5.4% and 5.1% of our total revenue, respectively. For
the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, we recorded selling and marketing
expenses of RMB18.0 million, RMB19.1 million and RMB21.1 million, respectively,
representing 1.8%, 1.7% and 1.2% of our total revenue, respectively.
As our business grows, we expect to continue to integrate technology including AI and
big-data tools into high-volume tasks and business operation, reducing dependency on
manual labor and improving the utilization of our personnel. We will continue to implement
technological services and refine team structures to support scalable growth with a leaner
workforce. Our ability to control expenses while maintaining quality and consistency of our
services and products remains critical to enhancing our overall financial performance.

Allowance for Expected Credit Loss of Receivables
Except for certain trade receivables from customers with specific credit risk that
management adopts an individual impairment assessment approach, our Group uses a
provision matrix to calculate ECLs for trade receivables. The loss allowances for receivables
are based on assumptions about risk of default and expected loss rates to determine the
expectedloss.OurGroupusesjudgmentinmakingtheseassumptionsandselectingtheinputs
to the impairment calculation. The historical loss rates are adjusted to reflect the
forward-lookinginformationonmacroeconomicfactorsaswellasthecreditratinganalysisof
respective customers and other external data which have impacts to the ability of the
customers to settle the receivables.
Our Group takes into account different macroeconomic scenarios in considering
forward-looking information domestically and abroad. Our Group regularly monitors and
reviews the key macroeconomic assumptions and parameters related to the calculation of
expected credit losses. Our Group has identified the Gross Domestic Product (“GDP”) of the
countriesinwhichitsellsitsgoodstobethemostrelevantfactors,andaccordinglyadjuststhe
historical loss rates based on expected changes in these factors.

Estimated Net Realizable Value of Inventories
In accordance with our Group’s accounting policy, our Group estimates net realizable
value of inventories based on specific facts and circumstances. For different types of
inventories, it requires the estimation of selling prices, costs of conversion, selling expenses
and the related tax expense to calculate the net realizable amount of inventories. For
inventoriesheldforexecutedsalescontracts,managementestimatesthenetrealizableamount
based on the contracted price. For raw materials and work-in-progress, management has
established a model in estimating the net realizable amount at which the inventories can be
realizable in the normal course of business after considering the manufacturing cycles,
production capacity and forecasts, estimated future conversion costs and selling prices.
Management also takes into account the price or cost fluctuations and other related matters
occurringaftertheendof thereportingperiodwhichreflectconditionsthatexistedattheend
of each reporting period.
It is reasonably possible that if there is a significant change in circumstances including
ourGroup’sbusinessandtheexternalenvironment,outcomeswouldbesignificantlyaffected.
Property, Plant and Equipment and Intangible Assets — Estimated Useful Lives and Residual
Values
OurGroupdeterminestheestimatedusefullivesandresidualvalues(if applicable)and
consequently the related depreciation or amortization charges for its property, plant and
equipment and intangible assets (excluding freehold land and goodwill). These estimates are
based on the historical experience, anticipated change of technology, market condition and
the actual consumptions of related assets. The depreciation or amortization charge will
increasewhenusefullivesarelessthanpreviouslyestimated.Inaddition,technicallyobsolete
or non-strategic assets that have been abandoned or sold will be written off or written down.
Actual economic lives may differ from estimated useful lives and actual residual values
maydifferfromestimatedresidualvalues.Periodicreviewcouldresultinchangeinusefullives
and residual values and therefore change in depreciation or amortization expense in future
periods.
Income Tax and Deferred Taxation
Estimation and judgment are required in determining the amount of the provision for
income tax. There are transactions and calculations for which the ultimate tax determination
is uncertain during the ordinary course of business. Where the final tax outcome of these
matters is different from the amounts that were initially recognized, such differences will
impact the income tax and deferred taxation provisions in the period in which such
determination is made.
Deferred tax assets are recognized for unused tax losses and deductible temporary
differences to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available against which
the losses and deductible temporary difference can be utilized. Significant estimation is
required in determining the recoverability of deferred tax assets.
In the event that future tax rules and regulations or related circumstances change,
adjustments to current and deferred taxation may be necessary which would impact on our
Group’s results or financial position.

Accounting Policies and Significant Judgments for Revenue Recognition
Our Group recognizes revenue when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied, i.e.,
when control of the goods or services underlying the particular performance obligation is
transferred to the customer.
If control of the goods and services transfers over time, revenue is recognized over the
period of the contract by reference to the progress towards complete satisfaction of that
performanceobligation.Otherwise,revenueisrecognizedatapointintimewhenthecustomer
obtains control of the goods and services.
When the consideration in a contract includes a variable amount, the amount of
considerationisestimatedtowhichourGroupwillbeentitledinexchangefortransferringthe
goods or services to the customer. The variable consideration is estimated at contract
inception and constrained until it is highly probable that a significant revenue reversal in the
amountof cumulativerevenuerecognizedwillnotoccurwhentheassociateduncertaintywith
the variable consideration is subsequently resolved.
If a customer pays consideration or our Company has a right to an amount of
consideration that is unconditional, before our Company transfers goods or services to the
customer, our Company presents the contract liability when the payment is made. A contract
liabilityisourCompany’sobligationtotransfergoodsorservicestoacustomerforwhichour
Company has received consideration (or an amount of consideration is due) from the
customer.
Products Revenue
Revenue from domestic sales of products shall be recognized based on the sales
contracts, settlement vouchers and other documents generally upon the completion of
products delivery and arriving at the named place of destination and acceptance by the
customers.Uponconfirmingtheacceptance,thecustomerhastherighttoselltheproductsat
its discretion and takes the risks of any price fluctuation and obsolescence and loss of the
products.
Revenue from overseas sales of products shall be recognized based on the sales
contracts, customs declaration form, bill of lading, and other documents upon completion of
customs declaration or shipping out of the port and arriving to the named port or place of
destination. Upon the completion of customs declaration and obtaining the bill of lading or
arrival to the named port or place of destination, the customer has the right to sell the
products at its discretion and takes the risks of any price fluctuation and obsolescence and
loss of the products.
For further information on revenue from contracts with customers, see Note 5 of the
Accountants’Report.

Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
Our gross profit represents revenue less cost of sales, and our gross profit margin
represents gross profit divided by revenue, expressed as a percentage. Our overall gross profit
margins are primarily affected by our cost control (particularly with respect to our cost of
procurement), product mix and business scale. For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024
and2025,ourgrossprofitwasRMB161.8million,RMB182.4millionandRMB280.2million,

Comparison between 2023 and 2024: Our overall gross profit margin remained the same
at 15.8% in 2023 and 2024.
• Small-size E-paper Display Module (<4 inches): The gross profit margin of our
small-size e-paper display modules increased from 15.1% in 2023 to 16.4% in
2024, notwithstanding a decline in average selling prices. This improvement in
gross profit margin was primarily attributable to (i) a significant increase in the
average selling price of black-and-white small-size e-paper display modules from
RMB14.1 to RMB25 per unit, which offset the impact of lower sales volume, (ii)
a favorable product mix shift driven by a substantial increase in sales of
four-colorsmall-sizee-paperdisplaymodules,despiteareductionintheiraverage
selling price, and (iii) enhanced manufacturing efficiency as our production scale
expandedasourfour-colorproductsbeganmassproductioninthesecondhalf of
2024.Thenegativeimpactfromthree-colorsmall-sizee-paperdisplaywaslimited
due to their modest decline in both sales volume and average selling price.
Collectively, these factors contributed to an overall increase in gross profit
margin despite lower average selling price.
• Mid-size E-paper Display Module (4-6 inches): The gross profit margin of our
mid-sizee-paperdisplaymodulesdecreasedfrom20.2%in2023to15.3%in2024,
despite an increase in overall sales volume and revenue. This decline in gross
profit margin was primarily attributable to (i) a significant reduction in the
average selling price of black-and-white mid-size e-paper display modules from
RMB50 to RMB30 per unit, while their sales volume only slightly decreased,
resulting in lower unit margins, (ii) the introduction of multi-color mid-size
e-paper display modules in 2024, which generally have lower margins during the
early stage of commercialization, and (iii) an overall decrease in average selling
pricedrivenbypriceadjustmentsforcertainthree-colormid-sizee-paperdisplay
modules. Although four-color mid-size e-paper display modules recorded a
substantial increase in sales volume at stable prices, their positive contribution
was insufficient to offset the adverse impact of price reductions and the lower
margin of newly introduced multi-color mid-size e-paper display modules.
• Large-size E-paper Display Module (>6 inches): The gross profit margin of
large-size e-paper display module (>6 inches) decreased from 6.9% in 2023 to
3.6%in2024.Suchdecreasewasprimarilyattributabletoreductionintheaverage
selling price of our three-color large-size e-paper display modules, which
accountedforasubstantialproportionof revenuefromlarge-sizee-paperdisplay
modules. The price reduction was mainly driven by product iteration, as we
enhanced promoting four-color large-size e-paper display modules in 2024. To
accelerate the clearance of existing inventory, we adjusted the pricing of
three-color large-size e-paper display modules, which in turn resulted in a lower
overall gross profit margin.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
One subsidiary of our Group was certified as a High and New Technology Enterprise
(“HNTE”) in December 2022 with validity until December 2025 and successfully renewed
such qualification for another three years. Accordingly, the preferential EIT rate of 15% was
applied during the Track Record Period based on the then expected re-grant of HNTE
certification. One other subsidiary of our Group obtained HNTE in 2024 and hence it was
entitled to a preferential EIT rate of 15% for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2025.
SuchqualificationissubjecttoreviewbytherelevanttaxauthorityinthePRCforeverythree
years.
According to the relevant laws and regulations promulgated by the State Taxation
Administration of the PRC, enterprises engaging in research and development activities are
entitled to claim 175% from 2018 onwards (subsequently raised to 200% from 2022 onwards)
of their research and development expenses incurred as tax deductible expenses when
determining their assessable profits for that year.
Hong Kong Profits Tax
Hong Kong profits tax had been provided for at the rate of 16.5% on the estimated
assessable profits for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025.
Vietnam Profits Tax
One subsidiary of our Group in Vietnam is subject to corporate income tax (“CIT”) at
the standard rate of 20%. The subsidiary qualified as a small enterprise (with annual revenue
exceeding VND 3 billion but not exceeding VND 50 billion in the preceding year) and
thereforeappliedapreferentialCITrateof 17%.Thesubsidiaryisentitledtoataxexemption
for the first two years, commencing from the first year of generating taxable income, and a
50% reduction for the next four years. No provision for the Vietnam corporate tax has been
made for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2025 as the Vietnam subsidiary has no
assessable profits for both such reporting periods.
OECD Pillar Two Model Rules
For details of our income tax exposure under OECD Pillar Two Model Rules, see Note
11(d) to the Accountants’Report.
OurincometaxexpenseincreasedfromRMB1.3millionin2024toRMB16.9millionin
2025 which was primarily due to the increase in our taxable income in 2025. Our income tax
expense decreased from RMB7.1 million in 2023 to RMB1.3 million in 2024, which was
primarily due to increased tax deduction for R&D expenses as a result of our increased R&D
expenses. For further details of our income tax expense, see Note 11 to the Accountants’
Report.

During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not
experience any significant difficulty in collecting trade receivables from customers.
To enhance our accounts receivable recovery process, we have adopted the following
measures:(a)requiringmanagementtoperformongoingcreditevaluationsof counterparties;
(b)establishingpoliciestoensurethatcredittermsaregrantedonlytocounterpartieswithan
appropriatecredithistory,(c)encouragingourrelevantbusinessstaff toproactivelyfollowup
on acceleration of payment collection and setting trade receivable collection rate as a key
performance indicator linked to staff bonus, and (d) issuing payment collection letters to
customers with significant overdue balances, and in the event of significant payment delays
after repeated collection attempts, we may resort to legal proceedings to collect the
outstanding amounts.
In addition, under our internal credit risk control policies: (a) the finance management
center sets clear standards for recognizing and measuring credit loss allowance and conducts
regular reviews of overdue receivables. It prepares schedules for credit loss allowance
adjustmentsforapprovalbyseniormanagementandtheboard;(b)businesspersonnelandthe
finance management center periodically reconcile receivable balances with customers to
confirm accuracy and promptly resolve discrepancies; (c) sales assistants prepare detailed
collection reports and follow up on overdue payments. International business managers and
senior executives review and approve collection actions, and all collection efforts are
documented;and(d)incasesof significantpaymentdelaysafterrepeatedcollectionattempts,
we may escalate the matter to legal proceedings to recover outstanding amounts.
Our Directors consider that there is no material recoverability issue with respect to
trade receivables aged over one year, and sufficient credit loss allowance has been made,
taking into account our enhanced credit risk management measures. Furthermore, our
Directors believe these measures are effective, as demonstrated by (i) a decreasing trend in
average trade receivables turnover days during the Track Record Period, (ii) a consistently
high proportion of trade receivables aged within one year during the Track Record Period,
and (iii) credit loss allowance representing a relatively smaller proportion of total trade
receivables over time.

RMB425.8 million as of April 30, 2026, primarily due to (i) the increase in inventories of
RMB79.9 million and (ii) the decrease in borrowings of RMB36.8 million, partially offset by
the increase in trade and notes payables of RMB60.7 million.
Our net current assets decreased from RMB442.9 million as of December 31, 2024 to
RMB367.7millionasof December31,2025,primarilydueto(i)theincreaseinborrowingsof
RMB228.3 million to support our continued expansion of operations and (ii) the increase in
trade and notes payables of RMB58.7 million, reflecting our business expansion, partially
offset by (i) the increase in inventories of RMB204.4 million, as we anticipated increased
demand for our products and (ii) the increase in trade and notes receivables of RMB111.3
million, resulting from our increased business scale.
Our net current assets decreased from RMB473.6 million as of December 31, 2023 to
RMB442.9 million as of December 31, 2024, primarily due to (i) the increase in trade and
notes payables of RMB92.1 million, reflecting our growing need for raw materials in
anticipation of growing demand of our products, (ii) the increase in the borrowings of
RMB47.9milliontosupportourcontinuedexpansionof operations,(iii)thedecreaseincash
and cash equivalents of RMB28.6 million, reflecting investment in our overseas business
expansion, partially offset by (i) the increase in inventories of RMB89.1 million and (ii) the
increase in trade and notes receivables of RMB59.6 million, both reflecting increased sales
volume of our products.

FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT
We are exposed to a variety of financial risks, including: (a) market risks (including
foreign exchange risks and interest rate risks), (b) credit risks and (c) liquidity risks. Our
overall risk management seeks a balance between risk and return, minimizes the adverse
impact of risk on our finance performance and maximizes the interests of shareholders and
otherequityinvestors.Basedonthisriskmanagementobjective,thebasicstrategyof ourrisk
managementistoidentifyandanalyzethevariousrisksfacedbyus,establishappropriaterisk
tolerance thresholds and timely and reliably supervise various risks to control them within a
limitedrange.Forfurtherdetailsof ourfinancialrisksandourfinancialriskmanagement,see
Note 3 to the Accountants’Report.
DIVIDENDS
We declared and paid dividends of RMB23.0 million in 2024. Other than that, no
dividend was declared or paid by our Company or any of our subsidiaries during the Track
Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date. Our dividend distribution record in the
past may not be used as a reference or basis to determine the level of dividends that may be
declared or paid by us in the future. Currently, our Group does not have a formal dividend
policy and does not have a predetermined dividend distribution ratio and do not intend to do
so following the Global Offering.
After completion of the Global Offering, we may distribute dividends in the form of
cash or by other means permitted by our Articles of Association. Any proposed distribution
of dividends shall be formulated by our Board and will be subject to approval of our
Shareholders. A decision to declare or to pay any dividends in the future, and the amount of
any dividend, will depend upon a number of factors, including our earnings and financial
condition, operating requirements, capital requirements, business prospects, statutory,
regulatoryandcontractualrestrictionsonourdeclarationandpaymentof dividends,andany
other factors that our Directors may consider important.
AsadvisedbyourPRCLegalAdvisorsandaccordingtothePRCCompanyLaw,aPRC
incorporated company is required to set aside at least 10% of its after-tax profits each year,
after making up previous years’accumulated losses, if any, to contribute to certain statutory
reserve funds until the aggregate amount contributed to such funds reaches 50% of its
registered capital. Such company may pay dividends out of after-tax profits after making up
for accumulated losses and contributing to statutory reserve funds as mentioned above.
As confirmed by our PRC Legal Advisors, according to relevant PRC laws, any future
netprofitthatourCompanyoranyof ourPRCsubsidiariesmakewillhavetobefirstapplied
to make up for any historically accumulated losses, after which we will be obliged to allocate
10% of net profit to our statutory common reserve fund until such fund has reached more
than50%of ourregisteredcapital.Wewillthereforeonlybeabletodeclaredividendsafter(i)
all our historically accumulated losses (if any) have been made up for; and (ii) we have
allocated sufficient net profit to our statutory common reserve fund as described above.

Commission and Expenses
Syndicate Members (as defined below) involved in the Global Offering (including all
Underwriters) will receive an underwriting commission of 3.0% of the aggregate Offer Price
of the Offer Shares (including any Offer Shares to be issued pursuant to the exercise of the
Over-allotment Option) (“Fixed Fees”). In addition, we may, at our sole and absolute
discretion, pay to the Syndicate Members an additional incentive fee of up to 1.0% of the
aggregateOfferPriceof theOfferShares(includinganyOfferSharestobeissuedpursuantto
the exercise of the Over-allotment Option) (“Discretionary Fees”). As of the date of this
prospectus, the allocation of a portion of the Fixed Fees remains subject to the Company’s
discretion. According to the Listing Rules, any unallocated portion of the Fixed Fees will be
regarded as discretionary fees. Accordingly, assuming the Discretionary Fees will be paid in
full, the ratio of the Fixed Fees and Discretionary Fees (as classified under and for the
purpose of Rule 3A.34 of the Listing Rules) payable by the Company to all Syndicate
Members(bothbeforeandaftertheexerciseof theOver-allotmentOption,if any)isexpected
to be 54.8:45.2. For unsubscribed Hong Kong Offer Shares reallocated to the International
Placing, we will pay an underwriting commission at the rate applicable to the International
Placing and such commission will be paid to the relevant International Underwriters and not

STABILIZATION
Stabilization is a practice used by underwriters in some markets to facilitate the
distributionof securities.Tostabilize,theunderwritersmaybidfor,orpurchase,thesecurities
in the secondary market, during a specified period of time, to retard and, if possible, prevent
a decline in the initial public market price of the securities below the Offer Price. Such
transactionsmaybeeffectedinalljurisdictionswhereitispermissibletodoso,ineachcasein
compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, including those of Hong
Kong.InHongKong,thepriceatwhichstabilizationiseffectedisnotpermittedtoexceedthe
Offer Price.

STRUCTURE OF THE GLOBAL OFFERING
In connection with the Global Offering, the Stabilizing Manager, or any person acting
for it, on behalf of the Underwriters, may over-allocate or effect transactions with a view to
stabilizing or supporting the market price of our H Shares at a level higher than that which
might otherwise prevail in the open market for a limited period after the Listing Date.
However, there is no obligation on the Stabilizing Manager or any persons acting for it to
conductanysuchstabilizingaction.Suchstabilizingaction,if taken,willbeconductedatthe
absolute discretion of the Stabilizing Manager or any person acting for it and may be
discontinuedatanytime,andisrequiredtobebroughttoanendonthe30thdayafterthelast
day for lodging applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering.
Stabilization action permitted in Hong Kong under the Securities and Futures (Price
Stabilizing) Rules of the SFO includes (i) over-allocating for the purpose of preventing or
minimizing any reduction in the market price of our H Shares, (ii) selling or agreeing to sell
our H Shares so as to establish a short position in them for the purpose of preventing or
minimizinganyreductioninthemarketpriceof ourHShares,(iii)purchasing,oragreeingto
purchase, our H Shares pursuant to the Over-allotment Option in order to close out any
positionestablishedunder(i)or(ii)above,(iv)purchasing,oragreeingtopurchase,anyof our
H Shares for the sole purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction in the market price
of our H Shares, (v) selling or agreeing to sell any H Shares in order to liquidate any position
established as a result of those purchases, and (vi) offering or attempting to do anything as
described in (ii), (iii), (iv) or (v) above.
Specifically, prospective applicants for and investors in H Shares should note that:
• the Stabilizing Manager (or any person acting for it) may, in connection with the
stabilizing action, maintain a long position in the H Shares;
• thereisnocertaintyastotheextenttowhichandthetimeorperiodforwhichthe
Stabilizing Manager (or any person acting for it) will maintain such a long
position;
• liquidation of any such long position by the Stabilizing Manager (or any person
acting for it) and selling in the open market may have an adverse impact on the
market price of the H Shares;
• no stabilizing action can be taken to support the price of the H Shares for longer
thanthestabilizingperiodwhichwillbeginontheListingDateandisexpectedto
expireonSunday,August2,2026beingthe30thdayafterthelastdayforlodging
applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering. After this date, when no
further action may be taken to support the price of the H Shares, demand for the
H Shares, and therefore the price of the H Shares, could fall;
• the price of the H Shares cannot be assured to stay at or above the Offer Price by
the taking of any stabilizing action; and
• stabilizingbidsortransactionseffectedinthecourseof thestabilizingactionmay
bemadeatanypriceatorbelowtheOfferPrice,whichmeansthatstabilizingbids
ortransactionseffectedmaybemadeatapricebelowthepricepaidbyapplicants
for, or investors in, the Offer Shares.
Inordertoeffectstabilizationactions,theStabilizingManagerwillarrangecoverof up
toanaggregateof 767,750HShares,representinguptoapproximately15%of theinitialOffer
Shares, through delayed delivery arrangements with investors who are allocated Offer Shares
in the International Placing. As of the date of this prospectus, no Offer Shares have been
allocated and no such arrangements have been entered into. The delayed delivery
arrangements (if specifically agreed by an investor) relate only to the delay in the delivery of
the Offer Shares to such investor and the Offer Price for the Offer Shares allocated to such
investor will be paid before the Listing Date. Both the size of such cover and the extent to

Option will not be exercised.
Our Company will ensure or procure that an announcement in compliance with the

the expiration of the stabilization period.

IFRS18PresentationandDisclosureinFinancialStatements
IFRS 18 “Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements”, which sets out requirements on
presentation and disclosures in financial statements, will replace IAS 1 “Presentation of Financial
Statements”.ThisnewIFRSAccountingStandard,whilecarryingforwardmanyof therequirements
in IAS 1, introduces new requirements to present specified categories and defined subtotals in the
statementof profitorloss;providedisclosuresonmanagement-definedperformancemeasuresinthe
notes to the financial statements and improve aggregation and disaggregation of information to be
disclosedinthefinancialstatements.Inaddition,someIAS1paragraphshavebeenmovedtoIAS8
“Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors” and IFRS 7 “Financial
Instruments: Disclosures”. Minor amendments to IAS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows” and IAS 33
“EarningsperShare”arealsomade.
IFRS 18, and amendments to other standards, will be effective for annual periods beginning on or
afterJanuary1,2027,withearlyapplicationpermitted.TheapplicationofIFRS18isnotexpectedto
have significant impact on the Group’s financial position and performance, but may affect the
presentationof thestatementof profitorlossanddisclosuresinthefuturefinancialstatements.

maximizetheinterestsof shareholdersandotherequityinvestors.Basedonthisriskmanagementobjective,
thebasicstrategyof theGroup’sriskmanagementistoidentifyandanalyzethevariousrisksfacedbythe

This note provides information on how the Group determines the fair values of various
financialassetsandliabilities.

basedonthedegreetowhichtheinputstothefairvaluemeasurementsareobservableandthe
significanceof theinputstothefairvaluemeasurementinitsentirety,whicharedescribedas
follows:
• Level1inputsarequotedprices(unadjusted)inactivemarketsforidenticalassetsor
liabilitiesthattheentitycanaccessatthemeasurementdate;
• Level2inputsareinputs,otherthanquotedpricesincludedwithinLevel1,thatare
observablefortheassetorliability,eitherdirectlyorindirectly;and
• Level3inputsareunobservableinputsfortheassetorliability.

4. CRITICALACCOUNTINGESTIMATESANDJUDGMENTS
The Group continually evaluates the critical accounting estimates and key judgments applied based on
historical experience and other factors, including expectations of future events that are believed to be
reasonable.
The critical accounting estimates and key assumptions that have a significant risk of causing a material
adjustmenttothecarryingamountsof assetsandliabilitiesareoutlinedbelow:
(a) AllowanceforExpectedCreditLossof Receivables
Exceptforcertaintradereceivablesfromcustomerswithspecificcreditriskthatmanagementadopts
anindividualimpairmentassessmentapproach,theGroupusesaprovisionmatrixtocalculateECLs
for trade receivables. The loss allowances for receivables are based on assumptions about risk of
defaultandexpectedlossratestodeterminetheexpectedloss.TheGroupusesjudgmentinmaking
theseassumptionsandselectingtheinputstotheimpairmentcalculation.Thehistoricallossratesare
adjusted to reflect the forward-looking information on macroeconomic factors as well as the credit
ratinganalysisof respectivecustomersandotherexternaldatawhichhaveimpactstotheabilityof
thecustomerstosettlethereceivables.
The Group takes into account different macroeconomic scenarios in considering forward-looking
information in Chinese mainland and abroad. The Group regularly monitors and reviews the key
macroeconomicassumptionsandparametersrelatedtothecalculationof expectedcreditlosses.The
GrouphasidentifiedtheGrossDomesticProduct(“GDP”)of thecountriesinwhichitsellsitsgoods
to be the most relevant factors, and accordingly adjusts the historical loss rates based on expected
changesinthesefactors.
(b) EstimatedNetRealizableValueof Inventories
In accordance with the Group’s accounting policy, the Group estimates net realizable value of
inventoriesbasedonspecificfactsandcircumstances.Fordifferenttypesofinventories,itrequiresthe
estimation on selling prices, costs of conversion, selling expenses and the related tax expense to
calculatethenetrealizableamountof inventories.Forinventoriesheldforexecutedsalescontracts,
managementestimatesthenetrealizableamountbasedonthecontractedprice.Forrawmaterialsand
work-in-progress, management has established a model in estimating the net realizable amount at
which the inventories can be realizable in the normal course of business after considering the
manufacturing cycles, production capacity and forecasts, estimated future conversion costs and
selling prices. Management also takes into account the price or cost fluctuations and other related
matters occurring after the end of the year which reflect conditions that existed at the end of each
year.
Itisreasonablypossiblethatif thereisasignificantchangeincircumstancesincludingtheGroup’s
businessandtheexternalenvironment,outcomeswouldbesignificantlyaffected.
(c) Property,PlantandEquipmentandIntangibleAssets—EstimatedUsefulLivesandResidualValues
TheGroupdeterminestheestimatedusefullivesandresidualvalues(if applicable)andconsequently
the related depreciation/amortization charges for its property, plant and equipment and intangible
assets(excludingfreeholdlandandgoodwill).Theseestimatesarebasedonthehistoricalexperience,
anticipated change of technology, market condition and the actual consumptions of related assets.
The depreciation/amortization charge will increase when useful lives are less than previously
estimated.Inaddition,technicallyobsoleteornon-strategicassetsthathavebeenabandonedorsold
willbewrittenoff orwrittendown.

=== PAGE 324 ===
APPENDIX I ACCOUNTANTS’ REPORT
Actual economic lives may differ from estimated useful lives and actual residual values may differ
from estimated residual values. Periodic review could result in change in useful lives and residual
valuesandthereforechangeindepreciation/amortizationexpenseinfutureperiods.
(d) IncomeTaxandDeferredTaxation
Estimation and judgment are required in determining the amount of the provision for income tax.
Therearetransactionsandcalculationsforwhichtheultimatetaxdeterminationisuncertainduring
the ordinary course of business. Where the final tax outcome of these matters is different from the
amountsthatwereinitiallyrecognized,suchdifferenceswillimpactontheincometaxanddeferred
taxationprovisionsintheperiodinwhichsuchdeterminationismade.
Deferredtaxassetsarerecognizedforunusedtaxlossesanddeductibletemporarydifferencestothe
extentthatitisprobablethattaxableprofitwillbeavailableagainstwhichthelossesanddeductible
temporary difference can be utilized. Significant estimation is required in determining the
recoverabilityof deferredtaxassets.
In the event that future tax rules and regulations or related circumstances change, adjustments to
current and deferred taxation may be necessary which would impact on the Group’s results or
financialposition.

(f) AccountingPoliciesandSignificantJudgmentsforRevenueRecognition
TheGrouprecognizesrevenuewhen(oras)aperformanceobligationissatisfied,i.e.,whencontrolof
thegoodsorservicesunderlyingtheparticularperformanceobligationistransferredtothecustomer.
If controlof thegoodsandservicestransfersovertime,revenueisrecognizedovertheperiodof the
contractbyreferencetotheprogresstowardscompletesatisfactionof thatperformanceobligation.
Otherwise,revenueisrecognizedatapointintimewhenthecustomerobtainscontrolof thegoods
andservices.
When the consideration in a contract includes a variable amount, the amount of consideration is
estimatedtowhichtheGroupwillbeentitledinexchangefortransferringthegoodsorservicestothe
customer. The variable consideration is estimated at contract inception and constrained until it is
highly probable that a significant revenue reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue recognized
will not occur when the associated uncertainty with the variable consideration is subsequently
resolved.
If acustomerpaysconsiderationortheCompanyhasarighttoanamountof considerationthatis
unconditional, before the Company transfers goods or services to the customer, the Company
presents the contract liability when the payment is made. A contract liability is the Company’s
obligation to transfer goods or services to a customer for which the Company has received
consideration(oranamountof considerationisdue)fromthecustomer.

expensesincurredastaxdeductibleexpenseswhendeterminingtheirassessableprofitsforthatyear

provideatemporaryexceptionfromdeferredtaxaccountingfortheincometaxarisingfromtaxlaw

The Group is within the scope of global minimum tax under the OECD Pillar Two model rules

40. SUMMARYOFOTHERACCOUNTINGPOLICIES
(1) Principlesof Consolidation
The Historical Financial Information incorporate the financial statements of the Company and
entities (including structured entities) controlled by the Company and its subsidiaries. Control is
achievedwhentheCompany:
• haspowerovertheinvestee;
• isexposed,orhasrights,tovariablereturnsfromitsinvolvementwiththeinvestee;and
• hastheabilitytouseitspowertoaffectitsreturns.
TheGroupreassesseswhetherornotitcontrolsaninvesteeif factsandcircumstancesindicatethat
therearechangestooneormoreof thethreeelementsof controllistedabove.
When the Group has less than a majority of the voting rights of an investee, it has power over the
investee when the voting rights are sufficient to give it the practical ability to direct the relevant
activities of the investee unilaterally. The Group considers all relevant facts and circumstances in
assessing whether or not the Group’s voting rights in an investee are sufficient to give it power,
including:
• thesizeof theGroup’sholdingof votingrightsrelativetothesizeanddispersionof holdings
of theothervoteholders;
• potentialvotingrightsheldbytheGroup,othervoteholdersorotherparties;
• rightsarisingfromothercontractualarrangements;and
• anyadditionalfactsandcircumstancesthatindicatethattheGrouphas,ordoesnothave,the
current ability to direct the relevant activities at the time that decisions need to be made,
includingvotingpatternsatpreviousshareholders’meetings.
Consolidation of a subsidiary begins when the Company obtains control over the subsidiary and
ceases when the Company loses control of the subsidiary. Specifically, income and expenses of a
subsidiary acquired or disposed of during the year are included in the consolidated statement of
profitorlossandconsolidatedstatementof comprehensiveincomefromthedatetheCompanygains
controluntilthedatewhentheCompanyceasestocontrolthesubsidiary.

(10) FinancialLiabilities

costs) and the redemption amount is recognized in profit or loss over the period of the borrowings
usingtheeffectiveinterestmethod.Feespaidontheestablishmentof loanfacilitiesarerecognizedas
transaction costs of the loan to the extent that it is probable that some or all of the facility will be
drawn down. In this case, the fee is deferred until the draw-down occurs. To the extent there is no
evidencethatitisprobablethatsomeorallof thefacilitywillbedrawndown,thefeeiscapitalizedas
aprepaymentforliquidityservicesandamortizedovertheperiodof thefacilitytowhichitrelates.
Borrowingsarederecognizedwhentheobligationspecifiedinthecontractisdischarged,cancelledor
expired.Thedifferencebetweenthecarryingamountofafinancialliabilitythathasbeenextinguished

Taxation of Security Holders
The taxation of income and capital gains of holders of H Shares is subject to the laws
and practices of the PRC and of jurisdictions in which holders of H Shares are resident or
otherwise subject to tax. The following summary of certain relevant taxation provisions is
based on current laws and practices in effect, and constitutes no predictions of changes or
adjustments to relevant laws or policies or any advice or suggestions thereunder. The
discussion does not deal with all possible tax consequences relating to an investment in the H
Shares or take into account the specific circumstances of any particular investors, some of
which may be subject to special rules. Accordingly, investors should consult their own tax
adviserregardingthetaxationof aninvestmentintheHShares.Thediscussionisbasedupon
current laws and relevant interpretations in effect as at the execution date of this prospectus,
all of which are subject to change or adjustment and may differ from our past practices.
The discussion below does not involve any issue concerning the PRC or Hong Kong
taxation other than income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty and estate duty. Prospective
investors are urged to consult their financial advisers regarding the PRC, Hong Kong and
other tax consequences of owning and disposing of H Shares.

Principal Taxation of Our Company in the PRC
Enterprise Income Tax
Pursuant to the EIT Law and the Implementation Regulation of the EIT Law of the
PRC, enterprises are classified into resident enterprises and non-resident enterprises. A
resident enterprise refers to an enterprise that is established inside China, or which is
establishedunderthelawof aforeigncountry(region)butwhoseactualofficeof management
is inside China. A non-resident enterprise refers to an enterprise established under the law of
a foreign country (region), whose actual institution of management is not inside China but
which has offices or establishments inside China; or which does not have any offices or
establishmentsinsideChinabuthasincomessourcedinChina.AccordingtotheEITLawand
related implementation regulations, the uniform tax rate for enterprise income tax is 25%.
Smallmeagre-profitenterprisesthatmeettheprescribedconditionsshallpayenterprise
income tax at a rate of 20%. Important high- and new-tech enterprises that are supported by
the state can enjoy a preferential enterprise income tax rate of 15%.

APPENDIX III TAXATION AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE
According to the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Law of the PRC on the
Administration of Tax Collection《( 中華人民共和國稅收徵收管理法實施細則》) promulgated
by the State Council on February 6, 2016 and coming into effect on the same day, taxpayers
eligible for tax reduction or exemption shall resume tax payment from the date following the
expiry date of the tax reduction or exemption. If there is a change in the requirements for tax
reduction or exemption, taxpayers shall report to tax authorities when filing tax returns.
Taxpayers shall fulfill tax payment liabilities according to law when they no longer meet the
requirements for tax reduction or exemption; if they fail to pay the tax according to law, tax
authorities shall pursue tax payment.
Value-added Tax
According to the Interim Regulations on Value-Added Tax of the PRC (the “VAT
Regulations”)《( 中華人民共和國增值稅暫行條例》（增值稅條例」)), which was promulgated by
the State Council on December 13, 1993 and last amended on November 19, 2017, and the

engageinthesaleof goods,theprovisionof processing,repairandreplacementservicesorthe
importation of goods in the PRC shall pay value-added tax. Except as otherwise provided in
the VAT Regulations, general taxpayers are subject to a VAT rate of 17% on the sale or
importation of goods; taxpayers are subject to a VAT rate of 17% on the provision of
processing,repairandreplacementservices;andtaxpayersaresubjecttoaVATrateof 0%on
the exportation of goods, unless otherwise provided.
PursuanttotheNotice36,thepilotprogramof replacingbusinesstaxwithvalue-added

thescopeof thepilotprogram,andthepaymentof businesstaxshallbereplacedbythepayment
of VAT, unless otherwise provided in the Implementation Measures for Replacing Business Tax
with Value Added Tax《( 營業稅改徵增值稅實施辦法》) in accordance with the Implementation
Measures.

andbecameeffectiveonMay1,2018,thetaxratesof 17%and11%originallyapplicabletothe

APPENDIX III TAXATION AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE
Foreign Exchange Policy of China
RMB is the legal currency of the PRC and is currently subject to foreign exchange
controls and cannot be freely inverted into foreign currency. The SAFE under the People’s
Bank of China is responsible for all matters relating to foreign exchange, including the
enforcement of exchange control regulations.
Under the Regulations on the Administration of Foreign Exchange of the PRC
(《中華人民共和國外匯管理條例》) issued by the State Council on January 29, 1996 and
effective from April 1, 1996, all international payments and transfers are classified into
current items and capital items. Approval by the foreign exchange authorities is not required
for most current items, but required for capital items. According to the Regulations on the
Administration of Foreign Exchange of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國外匯管理條例》) amended
on January 14, 1997 and August 5, 2008, the state does not impose restrictions on current
international payments and transfers.
Under the Administrative Regulations for Foreign Exchange Settlement, Sale and
Payment (Yin Fa [1996] No. 210)《( 結匯、售匯及付匯管理規定》(銀發[1996]210號)) issued by
the People’s Bank of China on June 20, 1996 and implemented from July 1, 1996, the existing
restrictions on foreign exchange transactions under capital items are retained, while the
remaining restrictions on foreign exchange conversion for current items are abolished.
According to the Announcement on Reforming the RMB Exchange Rate Regime
(《關於完善人民幣匯率形成機制改革的公告》(中國人民銀行公告[2005]第16號)) (People’s
Bankof ChinaAnnouncement[2005]No.16)issuedbythePeople’sBankof ChinaonJuly21,
2005 and effective from the same date, from July 21, 2005 onwards, China has implemented a
floating exchange rate system with management and regulation based on market supply and
demand and with reference to a basket of currencies. As a result, RMB exchange rates are no
longer pegged to USD. The People’s Bank of China publishes the closing prices of the
exchange rates of RMB against USD and other currencies in the interbank foreign exchange
market after the market closes on each working day, which serves as the mid-price for the
currency’s transactions against RMB on the following working day.
On August 5, 2008, the State Council promulgated the amended the Regulations on the
Administration of Foreign Exchange of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國外匯管理條例》), with
significantchangestoChina’sforeignexchangeregulatorysystem.Firstly,balancedtreatment
has been adopted for foreign exchange inflows and outflows. Foreign exchange earnings from
overseas may be transferred back to the PRC or deposited abroad, and foreign exchange and
settlement funds under capital items may only be used for the purposes approved by
competentauthoritiesandforeignexchangecontrolauthorities.Secondly,ithasimprovedthe
RMB exchange rate formation mechanism based on market supply and demand. Thirdly,
when there is or appears to be a serious imbalance in international balance of payments or
when there is or appears to be a serious crisis in the national economy, the state can take
necessary safeguard and control measures on international balance of payments. Fourthly, it
has strengthened the supervision and management of foreign exchange transactions and
granted extensive powers to the SAFE to enhance its supervision and management
capabilities.
According to relevant PRC laws and regulations, Chinese enterprises (including
foreign-investedenterprises)requiringforeignexchangeforcurrentaccounttransactionsmay,
without the approval of foreign exchange authorities, make payments through foreign
exchange accounts opened at designated foreign exchange banks, provided that valid receipts
or vouchers for the transactions are produced. Foreign-invested enterprises that need to
distribute profits in foreign currency to their shareholders and Chinese enterprises that need
to pay dividends in foreign currency to their shareholders may make payments from foreign
exchangeaccountsatdesignatedforeignexchangebanksorexchangeandpayatsuchbanksin
accordancewiththedecisionof theboardof directorsortheshareholders’generalmeetingon
the distribution of profits.
